The respondent No.1 in both two appeals contested the suit and that was decreed. 

 12. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgments and decrees of the trial Court; the defendant as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.536 of 2003 and Title Appeal No.337 of 2003 as appellant-defendant before the District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, the aforementioned -appeals were analogously heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Court No.6, Dhaka, who by his single judgment and decree dated 17.04.2004 allowed both the appeal and thereby set aside the judgments and decrees of the trial Court and decreed the suit No.255 of 2001 and dismissed the Suit No.296 of 2001. 

 16. Per, contra, Mr. A.M. Mahbub Uddin, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent in Civil Appeal N9.144 of 2008 and respondent No.1 in Civil Appeal No.145 of 2008 made submissions in supports of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He has submitted that the High Court Division have held that the Appellate Court below took the pains of going through the evidence adduced by the parties in support of their respective cases and then considering the evidence and assessing the evidentiary value of evidence of parties on the record and on careful scrutiny of the documents and the materials on the record coupled with the circumstances of the case found that deed as allegedly executed by Badrul Alam Chowdhury on 28.09.2000 was never acted upon, as such, the appellate Court below decreed the suit rightly after setting aside the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which have been affirmed by the High Court Division need not be interfered by this Division. He has further submitted that the High Court Division held that the appellate Court below also arrived at a finding that the alleged transfer executed by one Nila Islam and Badrul Alam Chowdhury, Attorney of Roksana Akhter Chowdhury to Rupayan Real Estate Ltd, vide sale deed dated 27.06.2001 was also a fictitious document which has never been acted upon by the parties. As such, the appellate Court below decreed the suit after setting the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court which have been affirmed by the High Court Division require no interference by this Division. He has finally submitted that the High Court Division observed that the appellate Court below on a careful scrutiny of all the materials and evidence on record have arrived at a finding that the plaintiff opposite party-respondent has been able to prove her case and the defendant petitioners as appellants have miserably failed to substantiate their case by any cogent evidence both oral and documentary and after taking into consideration all these material on record, the appellate Court below reversed the finding of the trial Court and allowed the appeal and decreed the suit of the respondent and dismissed the Title Suit No.296 of 2001 rightly and which was affirmed by the High Court Division by discharging the Rules. Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal. 

 20. We have gone through the testimony of the P. W.1, Rokshana After Chowdhury, it is crystal clear that, she could not say the name of the defendant She has filed the suit against the Managing Director of Rupayan Real Estate Ltd. and Badrul Alam Chowdhury. But, in her deposition, she never testified that Badrul Alam Chowdhury and Managing Director of Rupayan Real Estate Ltd. threatened her to dispossess/evict from the suit property. So, it is abundantly depicted that, the cause of action for permanent injunction against the Managing Director of Rupayan Real Estate and Badrul Alam Chowdhury never arose. The plaintiff of Title Suit No.255 of 2001, Rokshana Chowdhury although in a prayer prayed for declaration of title. On the same day, she has given the registered power of attorney being No.2166 dated 01.08.200.0. The attorney holder Badrul Alam. Chowdhury by didn't of that power of attorney transferred the Suit property to one Nila Chowdhury by registered deed No.3179 dated 23.11.2000 which was executed on 23.09.2000 and the plaintiff canceled the power of attorney through a deed being deed No.3229 dated 09.11.2000. The P.W.2 also could not improved the case of the plaintiff-appellant. 

 It is clear that a document that has been registered relates back to the date of its execution and when the question of title as between, the two contestants claiming on the basis of successive documents executed by the self-seine vendor Must be deter-mined with reference to the tide to the latter on the date of execution and not of registration." 

 25. The learned Advocate for the respondent orally argued that the date of execution was shown by the appellants giving antedate when disclosed the cancellation dated 23.11.2000. This argument has no legs to stand, because, in the plaint of Title Suit No.255 of 2001, there is no such averment. Not only that, at the time of testimony in Court, the P.W.1 even not a single word testified in this regard. 

 26. It further be mentioned that, in the prayer portion, the plaintiff of Title Suit No.255 of 2001 never prayed for declaration that, execution of the registered deed No.3229 dated 09.11.2000 was fraud, fraudulent and antedated, rather, simple declaration of title to the suit land. Moreso, the plaintiff respondent has failed to explain in the averment of the suit as well testimony, how she constructed the building in her portion of land nor disclosed about her funding system and sources. We are, therefore, of the considered view that the case of the plaintiff for declaration was not proved. The plaintiff respondent cannot get a decree in the suit for the lacking of the defence case. Rather, plaintiff respondent was not able to prove her own case by adducing independent, disinterested and neutral witnesses which is totally out of consideration of the High Court Division as well as Court of appeal below. 

 28. The trial Court, moreso, in the judgment opined that, on 06.11.2001, the defendant No.2 of this suit, filed a suit earlier being Title Suit No.296 of 2001 praying for declaration that, the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed No.2164 dated 01.08.2000 has no effective and binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff of Title Suit No.255 of 2001 as defendant of Title Suit No.296 of 2001, contested that suit by filing written statement. The earlier Suit No.296 of 2001 was decreed on contest by the trial Court vide judgment dated 31.05.2003 and appeal is pending against that judgment. Since competent Court of law has already declared that, the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed No.2164 has no effect and binding upon the plaintiff of earlier suit before passing the impugned judgment. Therefore, the plaintiff of Title Suit No.255 of 2001 cannot get a decree for declaration of title later on the basis of that registered Heba-bil-Ewaz deed No.2164 dated 01.08.2000 as observed in the finding of the trial Court. 

 30. Turning to discussing the same to prove the prayer of declaration of title and permanent injunction. The Court of appeal below without controverting the material findings and points at appeal not as per evidences on record discussed the matter, rather, extraneous matters were discussed and travelled beyond the points at issue in appeal. Therefore, the appellate Court's judgment suffers from legal infirmity which was also not looked at by the High Court Division. The High Court Division without dis-cussing any point as to the decree of the trial Court, as well as, failure of the Court of appeal bellow committed error of law in not reversing of such decree by the appellate Court from which it is abundantly clear that, the High Court Division was erred in law. 

 35. Accordingly, the Civil Appeal No.144 of 2008 is allowed. The judgment of the Court of appeal below arose out of Title Suit No.255 of 2001 is set aside. The Civil Appeal No.145 of 2008 is dismissed. Accordingly, the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below arose out of Title Suit No. 296 of 2001 is affirmed.

full_judgment:
3. The background leading to the Rule is that the land situated at present Sutrapur under SA Khatian No. 3105, Plot No. 7636 corresponding to RS Khatian No. 2283, Plot No. 11355 along with other land originally belonged to one Chandra Kanto Ghosh and Lalit Mohon Ghosh. Chandra Kanto Ghosh died leaving behind three sons namely Provat Chandra Ghosh, Satish Chandra Ghosh and Girish Chandra Ghosh and their names have been correctly prepared in CS Record-of-Rights. Girish Chandra Ghosh died leaving behind two sons namely Horpada Ghosh and Thakur Dhas Ghosh who sold their share to one Kusum Kumar Roy. Provat Chandra Ghosh made a gift of his share to his wife Labonnomoyee who instituted Title Suit No. 117 of 1932 in the Court of Second Sub-Judge, Dhaka for partition and in the final decree Satish. Chandra Ghosh obtained saham of the case land. Staish Chandra Ghosh died leaving behind his wife lndu Prova Ghosh and three sons namely Sunil Kumar Ghosh, Anil Kumar Ghosh and Ronjit Kumar Ghosh. By an amicable partition Suriil Kumar Ghosh became owner and possessor of the case land. In SA Khatian the name of Sunil Kumar appeared along with his brothers and mother. But they did not possess the case land (Annexure-'A'). 

 4. On 20-3-1974 Sunil Chandra Ghosh gifted the case land to his sister Niva Rani Guho Roy by a registered Deed No. 5807 and her name was correctly prepared in RS Khatian .No. 2283 (Annexure-`B'). Since the case land was declared as abandoned property as such Niva Rani Guho Roy filed Title Suit No. 520(A) of 1978 in the Court of First Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title. Said Suit was decreed ex-purls on 5-5-1981 (Annexure-'C'). 

 9. Next he submits that neither the petitioners nor their predecessors have ever migrated to India and the property in question has been recorded in the names of the predecessor of the petitioners as correctly published in CS, SA and RS Record-of-Rights. Title suit for declaration of title was decreed in favour of the petitioners and the court of Settlement allowed the case and ordered to exclude the property from the list of Abandoned Property and accordingly thereafter the Land Survey Tribunal by judgment ordered to record the property in the name of the petitioners who mutated their names in the Khatian and have been paying rents regularly to the government and, as such, the chain of title being well established, the petitioners are `মালিক' under section 2(da) of the Ain, 2001. That is the sum and substance of the submissions of the learned Senior Advocate Mr MI Farooqui. 

 More pertinently a declaration of title by and under mandate of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 does not change the vested character of the property. Vested character of the property will remain unharmed despite, that of the exparte judgment and decree of title as obtained by the petitioner." 

 19. Be it mentioned that in this case at the very outset the learned Attorney-General Mr AM Atninuddin- appeared and rebutted the first argument of Mr. Farooqui contending that the argument is erroneous in that the decree as it appears in Annexure-'C' to the petition relates to a suit for declaration of title and not a decree declaring the property not being a vested property. There is a certified copy of the original suit which is before us fortifies his submissions that the suit was for declaration of title. Therefore the learned Attorney-General submits that by no stretch of imagination the said decree would operate within the meaning of section 6(ka) of the Ain, 2001. The argument as it has been advanced by the learned Attorney-General have force. And the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General has also aided to that when he submitted that the mandate of section 42 of the specific relief Act, 1877 does not change the vested character of the property. Vested Character of the property will remain unharmed despite that of the exparte Judgment and decree as obtained by the petitioners. From that point of view the argument on this score by the Senior Counsel Mr MI Farooqui seems to be a fallacious one. 

 The crux of the matter is whether the disputed property is abandoned property within the meaning of Abandoned Property (Control, Management. and Disposal) Order, 1972 and that the whereabouts of the owners were not in this country on 28th February, 1972. On both counts the Court of Settlement found in affirmative. The first groilps of appellants are claiming the property by way of alienation after 28the February, 1972. In Government vs Orex Network Ltd., 10 ADC 1 = 17 BLC (AD) 196, the claimant claimed the property on the basis of oral gift followed by an affidavit acknowledging the gift on taking prior permission from the Ministry of Works for transfer, and the Ministry on accepting transfer fees muted the name of the claimant. Three of us (CJ, Md.Abdul Wahhab Mia and Syed Mahmud Hossain, JJ.) were members of the Bench in which it was held that "Admittedly. the. disputed property was published in the ‘Kha’ list of the abandoned buildings by Gazette Notification dated 23-9-19866.Therefore, all the permissions accorded by the Ministry or works and from 23-9-1986 allowing mutation  and transfer were void and those orders were obtained by collusion and fraud’. So, on this case also all the deeds and transfer were collusively made after PO 16 of 1972 came into force and these transfers are hit by Article 6 of PO 16 of 197. Similarly, Abdus Sobhan failed to substantiate his clean title and possession. He being a citizen of this country ought to have given explanation why he was not in possession why he was not in possession in 1972 has he been really inherited the same.”

parties:
Md. Anower Hossain ------------- Applicant-Petitioner.
Vs.
M.A. Nasir and others ----------- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
2.1 Facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that the Opposite Party No. 1, as applicant, filed Vested Property Tribunal Suit No. 247 of 2012 before the Vested Property Return Tribunal, Narayangonj and the said case was assigned to the Second Senior Assistant Judge and Arpita Shampatti Return Tribunal, Narayangonj for trial. The case of the opposite party-applicant in the said vested property case is that the suit land originally belonged to Ashok Ali Mir and, accordingly, C.S Khatian was published in his name. Ashok Ali died leaving behind his son Korom Ali Mir and two daughters, Atoronnessa and Oyasi Bibi. That, subsequently, the suit land was taken away by the Zaminder for non-payment of Khajana. Thereupon, Korom Ali and Atoronnessa, by paying Tk. 3,000/- as salami, became owner and possessor of the entire property. 

 2.4 While the said suit was proceeding, the petitioner school, represented by its Secretary, filed an application therein purportedly under Order 1, rule 10(2) read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and Section 25 of the Arpita Shampatti Prottarpon Ain, 2001 for adding it as party therein stating, inter-alia, that 906 decimals of land mentioned in the schedule to the said application along with other lands originally belonged to one Giris Chandra Das and others as owners of upper title as per C.S. Khatian 295, Plot Nos. 258, 281, 282, 583 under 154 Dapa Indrapur Mouza, Police Station and Sub registry Office Fatullah, Narayangonj and, under him, it was recorded in favour of one Ashok Ali Miah in the column of possession. That, because of the failure of payment of rent, the said property was returned to the Jamidar. That the said Jamidar, Giris Chandra Das, died leaving his five sons as heirs. That one of the sons, Narendra Nath Das, having died, Subod Chandra Das and Sushi! Chandra Das became heirs in his place and the said property was recorded under S.A. Khatian No.322 in the names of Surendra Mohor Das and others. That the said Surendra Mohor Das and others gifted the said property by an unregistered deed in favour of the petitioner-school and handed-over possession and, accordingly, the said 906 decimals land was recorded in the name of the Secretary of the School under R.S. Porcha. But certain property thereof was wrongly recorded in the name of Atorjanbibi, and the said Atorjanbibi then gifted the said property in favour of the said school vide registered deed No. 9245 dated 31.12.1974. Since then, the school has been possessing the said land upon erecting boundary wall and gate and that the school is run by a committee and functioning for about more than sixty years. 

 3.4 Fortunately, in the middle of hearing, we have found Mr. Probir Neogi, learned senior counsel, being virtually present before this Court, and sought his opinion on the issue of maintainability of civil revisional application against interlocutory orders passed by the Tribunal. Mr. Neogi has then referred to various provisions of the Arpito Shampatti Prottarpon Ain, 2001 starting with the preamble of the said Ain. According to him, the properties listed in the gazette are no more vested properties after the amendment done in 2013 vide Act No. 46 of 2013, rather the properties have become returnable properties. Therefore, the Tribunals and the Appellate Tribunals' function is now to determine the prima-facie owner of the said property and, accordingly, release the property on the application of the said prima-facie owner. However, by referring to Section 12 of the said Ain, he submits that even if the property is released in favour of a particular claimant or applicant, such release will not in any way be deemed to have given title or possession in his favour as per law, he submits. Therefore, he opines that, if there is any dispute as regards title and/or possession of the property concerned, such dispute has to be resolved by the civil courts in accordance with law. 

 4.2 As submitted by Mr. Probir Neogi, learned senior counsel, it appears from the very preamble of the said Act, namely Arpito Shampatti Prottarpon Ain, 2001, that this Act was in fact enacted by the Parliament in order for return of the properties, listed as vested properties, in favour of Bangladeshi original owners or their successors or successors in interest. Although some issues regarding vested property or returnable property are huge issues involving Constitution as well as our proclamation of independence, those issues may be dealt with in a proper case in future. For the purpose of this civil revisional application, it appears that the 'returnable properties,' or the `list of returnable properties' as defined by Clause-Ta' of Section 2 of the said Act, is the list which is published under Section 9 of the said Act.  Section 9 provides that the government shall publish a list of returnable properties through gazette in a particular way mentioned therein, and, according to Section 10, the owner of the said properties will be entitled to file application within certain period mentioned by law, or subsequent amendment to the law, before the Tribunal constituted by the said Act for release of the said properties. The Tribunal, thereupon, if satisfied that the claimant or the applicant has furnished enough supporting documents or evidences in support of his claim, will direct to release the said properties from the said list. 

 4.3 However, in deciding whether such properties should be released in favour of the said claimant or applicant, the Tribunal is required to determine whether the said claimant or applicant has established his prima-facie title in the said property, and this obligation of the Tribunal to determine prima-facie title becomes more relevant when we see sub-clause (Gha) of sub-section (8) of Section 10 of the said Act. However, if we read these provisions along with the provision of Section 12 of the said Act, it will become clear that such determination of ownership or title of a particular applicant or claimant is not the final decision as regards his title or possession. Section 12, clause (Kha) particularly, provides that any decision to release such property in favour of any person shall not be deemed to be a declaration of title or possession in his favour. This means that even after such release of the property in favour of a particular person treating him as prima-facie owner of the said property, anyone can challenge the title of that person in accordance with law before a competent civil court.

parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Dhaka and others ------ Appellants
vs
Tahera Begum, wife of late Md Serajul Islam and others --------  Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal are that one Md Mujtaba Siddique, son of late Mustafa Siddique was the original owner of the disputed property which was allotted to him by the Government of the then East Pakistan through a letter dated 23-1-1960. In pursuant to the aforesaid allotment letter, an agreement for lease of land measuring an area of 144 square yards or thereabout under the registration jurisdiction of Mohammadpur Sub-registry, Dhaka appertaining to Mouza-Baraba, Police Station-Tejgaon, now Mohammadpur, being Plot VI/15 in Block-D of the layout plan No.57 of 59/60 dated 6-8-1959 for a period of 99 years, was executed and registered on 26-1-1960 at the Sadar Sub-registrar Office, Dhaka being deed No.1542. Subsequently, the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique filed an application on 10-9-1963 praying for permission for constructing buildings thereon. The said original owner filed an application being No.1483 asking for a sanction of loan from the House Building Finance Corporation, Zonal Office, Dhaka and on 1 8-2-1964 the loan amounting to Taka 18,000 was granted in his favour. He also paid the Government dues in respect of his house amounting to Taka 18,000 and obtained a clearance certificate from the office of the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur, Mirpur Housing Estate, Mohammadpur, Dhaka being Memo No.550-AO dated 25-2-1964. The aforesaid original lessee, Md Mujtaba Siddique obtained a certificate from the Section Officer, LG Department and Government of the then East Pakistan, who attested his specimen signatures as genuine, which was put on the original lease deed. The original lessee on 28-2-1994 executed and registered .a mortgage deed being No. EP-36292 (deed No.1673) in favour of the House Building Finance Corporation to avail the loan sanctioned for the construction of building. The original lessee also maintained a telephone and had been paying monthly bills regularly, he obtained a certificate in respect of payment of the telephone bills being No.T.R./312048. The original lessee paid the municipal taxes regularly to the Dhaka Municipal Committee and he also paid the electricity charges and bills to the Dhaka Electric Supply regularly. The due rent was paid to the Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka. On 14-12-1972, a deed of sale being deed No.23424 was executed by the original lessee in favour of Md Serajul Islam, the predecessor of the respondents, Police Station-Keraniganj, District-Dhaka in respect of transfer of the case property situated at 6/15 Razia Sultana Road, Block-D, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka at a consideration of Taka 35,000. 

 7. Mr Biswajit Debnath, the learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing for the appellants, taking us through the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the relevant provisions of law, the connected materials on record submits that the whereabouts of the original owner of the property not being known and he having failed to own and possess the said property personally on the relevant date. The property was declared as abandoned property and vested to the Government as it was. He further submits that the date of sale deed dated 14-12-1972 registered by the original lessee is not legal as the said sale was hit by President's Order No.16 of 1972 and Ordinance No.LIV of 1985 and no title having been passed by the said deed, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. He also submits that the property having been published in the Bangladesh Gazette and the writ petitioners-respondents having failed to discharge the onus to the effect that, the property was not abandoned property, the High Court Division made an error of law in making the Rule absolute. He adds that the High Court Division sitting in writ jurisdiction not being the Court of appeal committed an error of law in interfering with the findings of fact passed by the Court of Settlement. 

 8. In reply, Mr Md Shahidul Islam, the learned Advocated appearing along with. Mr Qumrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents made submissions supporting the judgment and order of the High Court Division and prays for dismissal of the appeal and also submits that the Government Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate issued a notice to Mujtaba Siddique under its office memo No.608(68)/AO dated 15-11-1972 addressing the allottee of the House No.VI/ 15 Mohammadpur Housing Estate and requested him to pay other charges of the allotted house from January 1972 to onward, accordingly Md Mujtaba Siddique paid other charges for an amount of Taka 30 from January 1971 to December 1971 paid on 13-5-1972 under receipt No.1665 page No.41 and from January 1972 to December 1972 paid on 17-1 1 - 1 972 under receipt No.1672 page No.26. The original payment receipts were handed over to the predecessor of the respondents at the time of transfer of the case property. He further submits that the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique while living in the case house used to maintain a telephone whose number was 312048 and he paid the outstanding bill up to 1-12-1972. Accounts Officer, Telephone Revenue, Dacca issued a letter on 26-12-1972 requesting Mujtaba Siddique to pay the outstanding bill of the telephone No.312048. He also submits that with the promulgation of President's Order No.142 of 1972. 'The Bangladesh Transfer of Immovable Property (Temporary Provisions) Order, 1972 at the time of transfer, the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique swore an affidavit stating that the property proposed to be transferred does not come within the periphery of the President's Order No.16 of 1972 and is not an abandoned property. He adds that according to the promulgation of the President's Order No.16 of 1972, the specific claim of the Government of any abandoned property shall operate by operation of law with effect from 28-2-1972. But herein this case property following the Loan Case No.1483 dated 18-5-1964 implemented the President's Order No.7 of 1972 relating to the House Building Finance Corporation Mortgage Property. Following the above order, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works through its Director of Accommodation of the Government Officers Accommodation has referred his office memo No.10(899) Rent 78/1288 dated 10-1-1978. Making reference of the above letter, Section Officer of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, section-4 issued a later under its office memo No.Sha-4/1Ba-98/79 dated 3-2-1979 to the Director of Government Residential Accommodation, Directorate of Bangladesh Secretariate, Ramna, Dhaka stating that the rent should be maintained and borne under Head No.50 of the Besamoric Purta Karja Bhaban-`Kha' repairing under `Kha' 7 of the Fiscal Year 1978-79. This letter was forwarded to the Chief Accountant, General (Purta, Water, Electricity) Bangladesh, Dhaka by its office memo No.Shaka-4/98/79/ 183/1(2) dated 5-2-1979 and also the copy of the same was forwarded to the predecessor of the respondents Md Serajul Islam on 5-2-1979. He also submits that the original allottee Md Mujtaba Siddique also paid Taka 36 as tax to the Municipal Committee, Dhaka on 16-6-1970 with United Bank Limited, RIDC Branch, Dhaka. He again submits that the Government of East Pakistan now Bangladesh Office of the Administrative Officer, Mohammadpur Housing Estate issued a full payment clearance certificate under memo No.550 A/O dated 25-2-1964 and forwarded the same to the Assistant Commissioner of Relief Work (H&P) Department, Eden Building, Dhaka. A copy of the same was also forwarded to the lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique, son of late Md Mustafa Siddique. He again submits that before the loan was granted by the House Building Finance Corporation under Loan Case No.DA-1483 dated 18-5-1964, the Dhaka Improvement Trust was pleased to affirm a proposed extension on 'F' type QRTS No.VI/15 Razia Sultana Road, Block-D, Mohammadpur, Dhaka in favour of Md Mujtaba Siddique. Moreover, he submits that the lease deed No.1542 dated 26-1-1960 executed by the Government of erstwhile. East Pakistan through the Assistant Commissioner Relief Department and the lessee's thumb impression at the backside of the first page of the said lease deed dated 26-1-1960 exactly tallied with the thump impression of the subsequent sale deed No.23434 dated 14-12-1972. The said thumb impression of the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique is quite similar and exactly tallied with each other. Besides, he submits that there was no suppression of facts at the time of execution of the sale deed No.23434 dated 14-12-1972, which is evident that the vendor as the original owner has expressed the real fact of the payment of the installment money of the House Building Finance Corporation under Loan Case No.DA-1483 dated 18-5-1964. The said fact of the payment of the loan money was not disbelieved by the Government and the Director of Residential Accommodation, Ministry of Housing and Public Works. Following the smooth and regular payment of installment of House Building Finance Corporation, they desired to hire the case house from its owner Md Serajul Islam under memo No.18/79(899) Rent-78/1288 dated 10-2-1978. The First Court of Settlement, Dhaka did not consider the letter dated 10-1-1978 of the Director of the Government Officer, Residential Accommodation. Referring to that, Ministry of Works on 3-2-1979 issued a letter to Md Serajul Islam and both the letters were produced before the First Court of Settlement at the time of hearing on 29-5-2000, but the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka travelled beyond its jurisdiction stating that the respondents were asked to appear before the office of the Ministry of Works to decide regarding ownership of the case property which has been enlisted as abandoned property. Finally, he submits that the Honorable Appellate Division granted leave on 6-12-2009 relying upon the misconceived observation of the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka. Moreover, the leave granting order dated 6-12-2009 was against a dead respondent No. I , which has become abated. 

 i. Whether or not the deed of sale dated 14-12-1972 executed and registered by the original lessee was legal and whether the sale was hit by President's Order No.16 of 1972 and Ordinance No.L1V of 1985. 

 10. Now the first question arises regarding the legality of the sale deed dated 14-12-1972. From the materials on record, it appears that the original lessee got an allotment of the disputed property from the then East Pakistan Government for 99 years and the deed of lease was executed and registered on 26-1-1960 being lease deed No.1542. From Annexure-C, it appears that the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique on 18-2-1964 filed an application for sanction of loan from the House Building Finance Corporation, Zonal Office, Dhaka and the loan amounting to Taka 18,000 was granted in his favour. From memo No.550-AO dated 25-2-1964, it is found that he obtained a clearance certificate regarding the payment of Government dues in respect of his house amounting to Taka 18,000. The original lessee, Md Mujtaba Siddique obtained a certificate from the section Officer, LG Department and Government of the then East Pakistan having his specimen signatures attested as the signature was put in the original lease deed. The original lessee on 28-2-1994 executed and registered a mortgage deed being No. EP-36292 (deed No.1673) in favour of the House Building Finance Corporation to avail the loan sanctioned for the construction of building. From the materials on record, it appears that the original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique was in continuous possession of the suit property and had been paying the regular rent, telephone bills, electricity bills, municipal taxes etc. 

 11. The original lessee Md Mujtaba Siddique sold the property in question to Md Serajul Islam, the predecessor of the respondents by executing and registering a sale deed being No.23424 dated 14-12-1972. From the receipts of telephone bills, electricity bills, municipal taxes, it appears that at the time of executing the sale deed and delivering of possession thereof in favour of Md Serajul Islam as well as at the time of promulgation of President's Order No.16 of 1972, the original lessee was present in Bangladesh. It also appears before us from memo No.Sha-4/1BA-18/791183/ 1(2) dated 3-2-1979 that the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development hired the house in question from Md Serajul Islam for family accommodation of one of the Government officials which shows that since the purchase the predecessor of the respondent was in possession of the case land. 

 12. Article 7 of President's Order No.16 of 1972 and section 5 of the Ordinance No.LIV of 1985 have not been complied with. No notice has been served upon the original lessee or Md Serajul Islam, the predecessor of the respondents. As the original lessee was in possession of the suit land at the time of selling of the said land and thereafter, the predecessor of the respondents had been enjoying the possession of the same, thus the inclusion of the case property in the list of the abandoned buildings cannot be said to have been done legally rather it was done without lawful authority.

parties:
Naina Islam ------- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
14. A development of note as brought forth in the petitioner's second Supplementary Affidavit of 31-7-2016 occurred at this juncture. That is, on 8-2-1999 the Ministry of Land issued a notice directing the District Commissioner, Dhaka to take necessary steps to cancel the proceedings of LA Case No. 10/63-64 pursuant to the judgment dated 12-7-1979 in Writ Petition No. 835 of 1977. While parallel to these developments by the end of 1999 the petitioner, Mrs Naina Islam had already acquired a firm and entrenched title to the said property as above noted through a deed registered in her favour. 

 23. The Respondent Nos. 2 and 3 being RAJUK and its Chairman respectively are represented in these proceedings by their learned Advocate, Mr Md Imam Hasan. By filing an Affidavit-in-Opposition the said Respondents preliminarily assert that this Writ Petition is not maintainable. This stance predicated on their understanding that they have been divested of all responsibility regarding overseeing and protecting possessory and occupancy rights regarding the said property as early as on 23-12-1989 when the said plot was handed over to the original allottee, Dr. M. Rafiquzzaman. It is specifically submitted in that light that it remains the sole duty of the occupant-lessee in possession of the said property, i.e., someone in the position of the petitioner, Mrs Naina Islam to herself secure all rights incidental upon such possession and that in any case a matter of dispossession as this is to be agitated in a proper legal forum other one of judicial review as this. The Respondents have, however, not taken care to specify what other forum(s) may indeed be available to the petitioner in the circumstances. Having said that, the Affidavit-in-Opposition nevertheless reads to this Court as an attestation of all facts asserted by the petitioner as to her chain of title to the said property and the acquisition of such title through a permission of transfer from the original allottee granted by RAJUK itself. In other words, this Court notes at the outset, RAJUK asserts the petitioner's sole and exclusive right to control the said property and to exclude others therefrom. 

 27. The petitioner being aggrieved by RAJUK's volte face and inertia, has resultantly filed the instant Writ Petition for enforcement of her fundamental rights as protected under Article 42 of the Constitution. In this context, Mr Ajmalul Hossain submits that the petitioner, being a lessee of RAJUK, has the right to be in possession of the said property without let or hindrance, but the added Respondent No. 8 interfered with such possession by virtue of a deed purportedly executed by the original owners and also by virtue of a purported clearance certificate ostensibly issued by RAJUK in respect of the said property. 

 29. Mr Hossain submits that only the High Court Division can declare this inaction of RAJUK to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect as per article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution. Besides, it is only this Court that can issue an order in the manner of a writ in Mandamus directing RAJUK to evict the Respondent No. 8 from the said property and hand over the same to the petitioner, while exercising its special original jurisdiction under article 102(2)(a)(i) of the Constitution. 

 30. A yet more fundamental point is put forward by Mr Hossain. He argues that RAJUK is still the owner of the said property, whereas the petitioner is the lessee. The Respondent No. 8, Mr Mazumder who is alleged to have a registered deed in his favour from the original owner from whom the property was acquired for RAJUK, dispossessed the petitioner. The existence of the registered deed in favour of Mr Mazumder, according to Mr Hossain, does not bear relation to the legality of the lease in favour of the petitioner rather the same involves questions of RAJUK's title. Given that the said property was earlier acquired from Mr Mazumder's predecessor-in-interest, Mr Abdur Rahim, no residuary right vested in Mr Rahim after the acquisition process to transfer the said property to anyone. The acquisition process spelt an extinguishment of all of Mr Rahim's rights in the said property. Therefore, if at all, it is for RAJUK and not the petitioner to file a suit for declaration of its title over the said property. 

 32. If, on the other hand, the petitioner submits, the Respondents are hinting at the availability of alternate relief under, for example, the Specific Relief Act, 1877, then the remedy under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is not an equally alternative efficacious remedy as the same confining itself to recovery of possession stops short of determining the title to such property and, thereby, does not prevent initiation of satellite litigation. Furthermore, RAJUK itself has led the petitioner to apply before it and has acted upon such application for evicting the trespassers, albeit partially, without at any material time ever expressing its inability to dispossess the Respondent No. 8 trespasser. In the meantime, of course, the period of limitation for filing a section 9 suit for recovery of possession has elapsed. Therefore, even if for the sake of argument it is considered that a suit for recovery of possession is the proper remedy for the petitioner, the same could not be instituted due to the actions of RAJUK and due to the impression created and promise given by RAJUK that it will take steps to evict the Respondent No. 8 from the said property and restore the petitioner's possession of the same. 

 "The statutory rule under the common law is that the lessee is entitled to enjoy the properties leased out without interruption and there is an implied covenant that the lesser's title is such that no lawful entry, eviction or interruption will occur." 

 37. In the case of Ram Chandra Chatterjee vs Pramatha Nath Chatterjee reported in IC Vol. LXII! 758 it has been held that, "The landlord's undertaking for enjoyment by the tenant is implied from the relationship of landlord and tenant. [Transfer of Property Act, section 108 (c) Budd Scott vs Daniel (2), Markham vs Pagett (1)) and the undertaking would include the protection of the tenant from disturbance by the strangers claiming by title paramount." A similar view was taken in Syed Mukhtar Ahmad vs Rani Sunder Koer reported in CWN Vol. XVII Page 960 observing that, 

 "Sec. 108, Cl.(c) of the Transfer of Property Act is wide enough to include disturbance of possession by a person with a paramount title." 

 38. Here in the instant Writ Petition, the right to property of the petitioner is infringed by the Respondent No. 8, who purportedly has got a paramount title over the leased property from the person from whom the property was acquired by the Government for RAJUK and in whose favour RAJUK itself has purportedly issued a Clearance Certificate. So the Respondent No. 8 is not a complete stranger or a mere trespasser, rather he is a person claiming through a Clearance Certificate issued by RAJUK or claiming to have a paramount title over the leased property and the disturbance in the possession over the leased property by the Respondent No. 8 is a disturbance that falls within the provisions of section 108(A)(c) of the Transfer of Property Act. Therefore, RAJUK being the landlord and lessor has the obligation to ensure peaceful possession of the petitioner over the leased property by evicting the Respondent No.8 from the said property and putting the petitioner into the possession of the leased property. 

 41. The High Court Division in Sharping Matshajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. vs Bangladesh reported in 1982 BLD (HCD) 189 (Para 8) has observed that a promisee, acting in reliance on the promise, if suffers any detriment and alters his position and subsequently the promisor goes back on his promise the same is enforceable in writ jurisdiction. It is stated that where the government makes a promise knowing that it would be acted upon by the promisee and, in fact, the promisee acting in reliance alters his position, the government would be held bound by the promise and the promisee would be entitled to enforce the promise against the government. It has further been held that it is elementary in a republican government that the rule of law is supreme and no one, howsoever high or low is above the law. Everyone is subject to the law fully and completely as any other and the government is no exception. It is indeed the basis of constitutional democracy and rule of law that the government stands on the same footing as a private individual so far as the obligation of the law is concerned, the former is equally bound as the latter. The government cannot claim to be immune from the applicability of the rule of promissory estoppel and repudiate a promise made by it on the ground that such promise fetters its future executive action. If the government does not want its freedom of executive action to be hampered or restricted, the government need not make a promise knowing or intending that it would be acted on by the promisee and the promisee would alter his position relying upon it. But if the government makes such a promise and the promisee acts in reliance upon it and alters its position, there is no reason why the government should not be compelled to make good such promise like any other private individual. In the instant facts and circumstances, this Court finds this reasoning on the applicability of the Doctrine of Promissory Estoppel to be unqualifiedly securing the present petitioner from the adverse consequences of the erratic conduct of RAJUK.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1028 of 2018
parties:
Abdul Kader Howlader and others -------- Petitioners

-Vs-

Chan Miah and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present respondents as plaintiffs instituted. Title Suit No.94 of 2016 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 passed by the First Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna in Title Suit No.10 of 2009. In the suit, the plaintiffs, on 10.01.2017, filed an application for staying further proceedings of Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court rejected such application for stay and also dis-missed the suit summarily at this initial stage stating that the suit is not maintain-able. Against such order of dismissal, the plaintiff who was defendant in partition suit being No.10 of 2009 moved before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was made absolute subsequently. The plaintiff in original suit being No.10 of 2009 as petitioner filed the present petition for leave to appeal. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that the suit lands originally belonged to Chhaferuddin, Hochanuddin and others. Their names were correctly recorded in CS Khatian mentioning their respective shares. The said recorded tenants and Hochanuddin while enjoying and possessing the suit land, Hochanuddin died leaving behind two wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi and Kadbhanu Bibi. Kadbhanu Bibi gave birth to one son, namely, Amzat Ali and three daughters, namely, Bibishan, Kulsum and Orful. Other wife, Chhahera Bibi gave birth to two sons, namely, Afchher Ali and Hazrat Ali and 4(four) daughters, namely, Gedi Bibi, Duli Bibi, Barojan, Alekjan. One of the wives, namely, Chhahera Bibi got married to a recorded tenant, Chhaferuddin. The daughter of Hochanuddin named Bibishan died leaving behind 4(four) daughters, namely, Hamida, Rokeya, Rahila and Habibunnessa along with mother named Kadbhanu, one brother Amzad Ali and two sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful. Kulsum died leaving behind her full sister, Orful Bibi and step brother Hazrat Ali and Orful Bibi died leaving behind only son, Abdur Rahim and only daughter, Chherjan Bibi. Amzad Ali died leaving behind his mother, Kadbhanu, two full sisters, namely, Kulsum and Orful Bibi. 

 7. The CS recorded tenant, Yasinuddin while enjoying and possessing his share died leaving behind his mother, Chherbhanu, two full brothers, namely, Dalu and Lalu as his legal heirs. Said Chherbhanu died leaving behind her two sons, namely, Dalu and Lalu. Lalu died leaving behind his four sons, namely, Abdul, Ganjar, Chhattar, Rakmon and two daughters, namely, Bibishan and Sufia. Said recorded tenant, Yasinuddin died leaving behind his heirs, Abdul Jabbar and others and they have instituted Title Suit No.187 of 1977 before the then Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Barguna and the said suit was dismissed on contest and an appeal bearing No.65 of 1987 was being preferred which had been allowed and the defendants preferred Civil Revision No.2759 of 1996 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which was discharged on 29.10.2007. 

 9. The partition suit being No.10 of 2009 was decreed ex-parte on 25.09.2012 passed by the trial Court. The present respondents as plaintiff filed the present regular suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree dated 25.09.2012 on the ground of non service of summons in which the present respondent filed an application for staying further proceeding of Title Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out Title Suit No.10 of 2009. The learned Judge of the trial Court has rejected not only the application for stay but also dis-missed the suit as being non-maintainable. 

 10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No.37 of 2017 before the High Court Division, the High Court Division after hearing the appeal allowed the same setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10.01.2017 and thereby restored the original suit being No.94 of 2016. 

 12. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits present respondents as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside an ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not duly served upon them in the original suit and the plaintiffs (present respondents) filed an application for staying the execution proceeding Title Execution being No.04 of 2015 arising out from Titles Suit No. 10 of 2009 and only point for determination for the trial Court to ascertain as to whether the said application for staying would be sustainable. He further submits that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.10 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barguna for partition of the suit lands impleading present respondents and others as defendants. Wherein several sets of the defendants contested the said partition suit including the full brother of present respondent named Sona Miah after receiving the summonses of the Court, but the present respondents (plaintiffs in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) did not contest the said suit though the summonses were duly served upon them and it is evident from the decree of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 that the addresses of all defendants are the same and they are residing in the same mess and the preliminary decree of the said suit made final, but respondent Nos.1-3 instituted subsequent Title Suit No.94 of 2016 long delay and on the mere plea that the summonses were not duly served upon them by suppressing the material facts and as such, the trial Court rightly dismissed the suit, but the High Court Division passed an order of restoration of original suit after setting aside the order of trial Court. The learned Counsel further submits that admittedly the judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 has been challenged by one defendant named Abdur Rahman in Title Appeal No.69 of 2012 impleading the present defendants as respondent Nos.9-20 in the said title appeal by mentioning their addresses and their summonses have been duly served in the said title appeal, but they are reluctant to proceed with the said appeal and at a stage, the said appeal is dismissed affirming those of the trial Court and accordingly, the preliminary judgment and decree of the trial Court is made final and the defendants of the original partition suit tried to create an obstacle to enjoy the fruit of the said judgment and decree passed in favour of the plaintiffs by filing the vexatious suit and the trial Court rightly dismissed the same, but the High Court Division as the appellate Court without going through materials on record very illegally restored the original suit being No.10 of 2009 after setting aside the well-founded judgment and decree. He finally submits that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009; the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018. 

 15. Title Suit No.10 of 2009 was a partition suit instituted by the present petitioners as plaintiffs against the present respondents, Chan Miah and others and that summonses and notices were alleged to have been duly served upon all the defendants of that suit and thereafter, the suit has been decreed against defendant Nos.12/33/61-- -71/78/72/36/38/80-42/37 on contest and ex-parte against the rests. The defendant (in Title Suit No.94 of 2016) i.e. present petitioners have come with an allegation that the allegation regarding non-service of summons does not hold any water whereas present respondents, Chart Mia and others filed Title Suit No.94 of 2016 claiming that due to non-service of summons decree passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 is illegal, inoperative and liable to be set aside. 

 16. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the present petitioners argued that although on the ground of non-service of summons, defendant Nos.1 to 3 of Title Suit No.10 of 2009 instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 against the present petitioners, but they were duly served with summonses and notices. He further adds that the brother of plaintiff No.1, Chan Mia appeared and contested Title Suit No.10 of 2009 whereas the three plaintiff-respondent demanded that they were not ever served with summonses and notices. He further adds that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation and as such, that suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. He also argued that Title Suit No.94 of 2016 is not maintainable without challenging the final decree passed in Decree Execution Case No.04 of 2016 arising out of judgment and decree dated 25.09.2012 passed in Title Suit No.10 of 2009 and as an appellate Court, the High Court Division ought to have considered the said moot question in deciding First Appeal No.37 of 2017, but most illegally setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.01.2018 and as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 20. On perusal of the materials on record, it transpires that the plaintiffs (defendant in Title Suit No.10 of 2009) instituted Title Suit No.94 of 2016 for setting aside the ex-parte decree on the ground that summonses were not served upon them in that suit. The only point assigned in the impugned judgment and order is whether the execution case of the former suit should be stayed or not? But the learned Judge of the trial Court in course of deciding the fate of stay petition has dismissed the suit summarily. The learned Judge of the trial Court finds in the following verbatim:- 

 21. Now the question that falls for determination as to how far the trial Court is justified in dismissing the suit summarily in course of deciding an application for staying the further proceeding of Title Execution No.04 of 2015.
