lawyer:
Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate with Faruk Ahmed, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellants. 
Dr. Kazi Aktar Hamid, Senior Advocate instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent Nos. 1-7. 
None Represented—For the Respondent Nos.8-15.
parties:
Shahidul Haque being dead his heirs: Fatema Begum and others --------- Appellants
vs
Md Fazal Miah and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated the 24th day of November, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3505 of 2007 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-7-2007 passed by the Joint District Judge, Brahmanbaria in Other Appeal No.53 of 2006 allowing the appeal and reversing those dated 10-5-2006 in Other Suit No.71 of 2005 of trial Court. 2. The facts relevant to dispose of the appeal, in short, are that respondent No. 1-9 as the plaintiffs instituted Other SuitNo.71 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. The case of the plaintiffs was that CS Khatian No.114 in respect of the disputed land was prepared in the name of their predecessor-in-interest. CS recorded 'Ka' group tenants, Zalfur Uddin, Patchu, father of Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin, father of Lai Mahmud, were full brothers. Zalfur Uddin died issueless leaving two full brothers: Patchu and Kalfur Uddin as his heirs and accordingly, they inherited the share of Zalfur Uddin in the suit plots. Subsequently, Patchu died leaving behind his son, Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin died leaving behind his son, Lai Mahmud. The CS recorded tenants. Bashu .Miah died leaving behind plaintiff No.9 as his heir and Seraj Ali died leaving behind his three sons: plaintiff Nos.6 and 7 and Sultan Meah, father of plaintiff No.8. Kala Miah died leaving behind his two sons and two daughters: plaintiff Nos.4, 5, 10 and 11. Lal Mahmud died leaving behind his son named Abdul Khaleque. Thereafter, Abdul Khaleque died leaving behind his three sons and three daughters: plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 12-14. Thus, the plaintiffs became the owners of the suit land and some other lands. The suit land was correctly recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and in the name of their predecessor-in-interest during the SA operation. The plaintiffs had been possessing the suit land for a long time through their bargader, defendant No. l. Since the plaintiffs had to stay outside the area in connection with their business, defendant No.1 was entrusted to get the suit land recorded in their names during Bangladesh Survey. The plaintiffs recently came to know that defendant No.1 had been planning to construct houses on the suit land by filling it up with earth. Thereafter, the plaintiffs made a search of their khatian in the survey office and found that defendant No.1 had got DP Khatian No. 1107 in respect of the suit land along with some other lands recorded in his name. The plaintiffs asked defendant No.1 on 28-1-2005 to quit the possession of the suit land, but defendant No.1 refused to do so and instead, he claimed his title over the same. Thus, a cloud was created on the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land hence, they filed the suit for the relief as aforementioned. 

 3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that he was never a bargader in the suit land under the plaintiffs. He took settlement of some portion of the suit land from one Abdul Malek Haji and that he had been possessing the same. One Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury being the owner had been possessing 121/2 decimals land in Suit Plot Nos.434, 435 and 436 by way of purchase from the CS recorded tenants and sold the same to Kashem Ali and Sadir Meah by a registered kabala being No.7791 dated 6-10-1984. Besides Abdul Khaleque, the plaintiffs' father sold 2½ decimals land from Plot No.434 by registered deed No.37094 dated 3-4-1961. Sadir Meah sold 6¼ decimals land from the suit plots to Tuku Meah, Abu Bakar, Bazlu Meah and delivered possession thereof to them. SA Khatian No.112 was prepared in the names of Tuku Meah and other sons of Kala Meah. Tuku Meah, Abu Bakar, Nurul Huq and Bazlu Meah by a registered exchange deed bearing No.6973 dated 28-10-1958 exchanged 6¼ decimals land of the suit plots with Kashem Ali and delivered possession and thus, they became disinterested in the suit plots. Kashem Ali became owner of the entire suit land and he being in possession thereof sold the same to Zaher Meah by a registered deed being No.224 executed on 9-1-1977 and registered on 18-1-1977 and delivered possession of the transferred land to him. Zaher Meah exchanged the suit land with defendant No.1 by a registered exchange deed dated 13-6-1988. In this way, defendant No.1 became the owner of the suit land and had been possessing the same by growing crops thereon and by paying rents regularly to the Government. The plaintiffs having no right, title and possession in the suit land were not entitled to get any relief in the suit and the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Counsel, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the Appellate Court below being the last Court of fact failed to appreciate that the appellant is the purchaser of the land from the true owner of the suit land and they are not the Borgadar under the present respondent whereas the trial Court rightly held the aforesaid fact and dismissed the suit. He further adds that the positive findings of the trial Court were not adverted by the Appellate Court below who wrongly held that the appellants are liable to be evicted from the suit land although DP Khatian has been prepared in the name of the defendant-appellants on the basis of their title and possession for more than 12 years and, as such, the defendants acquired statutory right by way of adverse possession. He further adds that the revisional Court also failed to appreciate the aforesaid fact of right, title and possession of the defendant- appellants and wrongly supported the Appellate Court below which are the product of mere non-consideration, misreading and non-appreciation of the evidence on record. 

 10. He further adds that the trial Court failed to appreciate the evidentiary value of CS and SA Khatian which created an unrebuttable presumption in favour of the plaintiff and also that Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury had no saleable interest in the suit land and the defendants have failed to prove the very basis of preparation of the DP Khatian. He further adds that the DP Khatian and the rent receipt conferred no title. 

 12. It is admitted by the parties that CS Khatian No.114 in respect of the disputed land was prepared in the name of plaintiffs predecessor-in-interest. CS recorded "Ka" group tenants Zalfur Uddin, Patchu, father of Kala Miah and Kalfur Uddin, father of Lai Mahmud were full brothers and that Zalfur Uddin died issueless leaving two full brothers, Patchu and Kalfur Uddin as his heirs and accordingly, they inherited the share of Zalfur Uddin in the suit plots. It is not denied that subsequently, Patchu died leaving behind his son, Kala Miah and that Kalfur Uddin died leaving behind his son, Lai Mahmud. It is also undisputed that the other CS recorded tenants, Bashu Miah died leaving behind plaintiff No.9 and Seraj Ali died leaving behind of plaintiff Nos.6 and 7 and Sultan, father of plaintiff No.8 and Kala Miah died leaving behind his two sons and two daughters, plaintiff Nos.4, 5, 10 and 11 and that Lai Mahmud died leaving behind his son, Abdul Khaleque. It is also not denied that Abdul Khaleque died leaving behind his three sons and three daughters: plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and 12-14 and in this way, the plaintiffs claimed to have acquired the suit land and some other lands. It appears that the suit land was recorded in the names of the plaintiffs and in the name of their predecessor-in-interest during the SA operation. The plaintiffs also claimed that they had been possessing the suit land for a long time through their bragader, defendant No. l. It is also contended that since the plaintiffs had to stay outside the area in connection with their business, defendant No. 1 was entrusted to get the suit land recorded in their names during Bangladesh Survey and that the plaintiffs recently came to know that defendant No. l had been planning to construct house on the suit land by filling it up with earth. 

 13. The plaintiffs (respondents) have come with an allegation that they made a search of their khatian in the survey office and found that defendant No. 1 got his name recorded in DP Khatian No.l 107 in respect of the suit land along with some other lands. The plaintiffs asked defendant No.1 on 28-1-2005 to vacate the possession of the suit land, but defendant No.1 on the event of refusal to do so and instead of vacating, he claimed his title over the same. 

 14. On the other hand, the present appellants (defendants) filed RoR Khatian No.1 12 (Exhibit-Gha') from which it is seen that the name of Bazlu Mia, Nurubaksha, Tuku Mia and Abu Bakar son of Kala Gazi are the recorded tenants who are the successive heirs of CS tenant Bashu. The present, plaintiffs filed an exchange deed being No.6973 dated 28-10-1956 (Exhibit-Gail) from which it revealed that the aforesaid successive heirs of Bashu (who appears to be RS tenant) exchanged the suit property with one Kashem Ali and the suit property has fallen in the share of the second party, Kashem Ali through this exchange deed. The appellants (defendants) has filed another kabala dated 9-1-1977 executed by Kashem Ali (Exhibit-Ga) from which it appears that the suit property has been sold by Kashem Ali in favour of Zaher Mia (DW 3). Thereafter, the present appellants (defendants) filed another deed of exchange dated 13-6-1988 (Exhibit-Kha) from which it is seen that aforementioned Zaher Mia exchanged the suit property with Shahidul Haque who is the present defendant. On perusal of those registered deeds, it appears that the successive heirs of Bashu transferred their share in favour of the present defendants. It is admitted by the respondents (plaintiffs) that they have been possessing the suit land through their borgadar, defendant No. 1 which has been denied by defendant No. 1. But the said defendant claimed that he has been possessing the suit land for more than 17/18 years and thereby he has acquired a statutory right by way of adverse possession. 

 17. Defendant No.1 while deposing as DW 1 stated that certain portion of the suit land belonged to one Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury who granted settlement of such land to one Haji Khaleque and he transferred the said land to One Kashem Ali in the benami of Tawkin Mia and Shadek Mia who exchanged the same in favour of Zaher Ali and he subsequently exchanged such land with him (defendant No. 1). Aforesaid Zaher Mia while deposing as DW3 slated that he transferred the land in favour defendant No.1, but he could not say as to which land he has transferred. The learned Judge of the trial Court held that the defendant filed a RoR porcha. But there is no record which Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury was CS recorded tenant. The RoR is not a document of title. The Appellate Court observed that the name of Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury does not appear as the recorded tenant either in CS Khatian No.114 or kabala dated 6-10-1984. If Jogendra Mohan Chowdhury's title and possession in the suit land remained unproved, the purchaser (defendant) has acquired no title and possession. This observation made by the Appellate Court below has been approved by the revisional Court. We also find that Jogandra Mohan Chowdhury was not CS record tenant. The appellant (defendant) thus acquired no right and title in respect of such portion of land. Excepting such portion of land which defendant No.1 claimed to have been acquired from Jogendra Mohan, the appellant acquired other portion of the suit land as has been discussed by us earlier. In that case, we are of the view that the present appellant and respondent appears to be co-sharers in the suit jams and in that case, the respondent may be allowed to remain in joint possession with defendant No. 1.

caseno: First Appeal No. 71 of 2016 with Civil Rule No. 119(F) of 2016.
parties:
Eastern Food (Pvt.) Ltd. -------- Defendant No.3- Appellant

VS.

MNH Bulu and others -------- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J : This appeal at the instance of the defendant No.3-Eastern Food (Pvt.) Limited has been preferred against the judgment and decree dated 4-2-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 decreeing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract on compromise. 

 3. The respondent No. 1 MNH Bulu as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka on 7-2-2008 seeking a decree for Specific Perfor-mance of Contract impleading the respondent No. 2 Mrs. Hosn-e-Ara and respondent No. 3 Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakkha (RAJUK), Dhaka as defendants. 

 4. The plaint case, in short, is that the suit plot morefully described in the schedule of the plaint belonged to Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) now Rajuk; that Late Abu Ahmed Shah, husband of Hosn-e-Ara, defendant No. I got allotment of 15 khatas, 14 chattak land of plot No. CWN (B) 28 of Gulshan Model Town from DIT by allotment letter contained in memo No. 2725 dated 7-4-1962, subsequently on the prayer of the original allotee, Dhaka Improvement Trust DIT allowed the prayer accordingly Lease Agreement was executed between the defendant No. 1 and DIT by registered Lease Deed No. 8832 dated 22-9-1964; that after obtaining approval of construction plan by the DIT, defendant No.1 constructed a one-storied building upon the said plot taking loan from the East Pakistan House Building Finance Corporation by mortgaging the plot and had been residing thereon; that after libration war said plot was enlisted in the `kha' list of the abandoned property under President Order No. 16 of 1972 (PO 16 of 1972); that the defendant No. 1 filed Settlement Case No. 360 of 1995 in the Court of Settlement releasing the said property from the list of abandoned property. After hearing, the case was allowed and the government was directed to release her property from the list of abandoned property by judgment and order dated 29-6-1996. Against the order of the court of settlement, the government filed Writ Petition No. 710 of 2002 in the Hon'ble High Court Division, after hearing the said writ petition was discharged and judgment of the court of settlement was upheld; that the defendant No. 1 expressed her desire to sell the suit plot due to necessity and plaintiff agreed to purchase the same, after discussions between them, defendant No. 1 entered into an Bainanama Agreement for sale of the suit land and building at .a total consideration of Taka 4 core and out of total consideration money, defendant No. 1 received Taka 3 core 90 lac as earnest money (Baina Money) from the plaintiff and executed a registered Bainanama Agreement being No. 6359 dated 3-4-2006. That further case of the plaintiff is that an application was filed on 4-12-2001 for publication of Gazette Notification for release of the suit property from the `kha' list of Abandoned Property. Ultimately gazette notification was published on 6-9-2007 after much effort and great contribution and .help made by the plaintiff. That the plaintiff after publication of the gazette notification on 6-9-2007, the plaintiff repeatedly requested the defendant No. 1 to execute and register the sale deed on receipt of the balance consideration money Taka 10 lac; that inspite of repeated demand by the plaintiff, the defendant No. I did not execute and register the kabala. Finally on 23-10-2007, the plaintiff requested the defendant No. 1 to execute and register the kabala deed but defendant No. 1 informed that if the plaintiff did not increase the price of the suit plot in addition to balance consideration money she will not execute and register the sale deed. Hence the suit. 

 5. At the, time of filing of the suit on 7-2-2008, plaintiff by firisty filed two documents namely (i) Photocopy of the certified copy of the registered Bainanama No. 6359 dated 6-4-2006 (ii) Original Bangladesh Bank Chalan No. 8308 dated 6-2-2008 showing payment of balance consideration money Taka 10 lac. 

 7. Defendant No. 2 RAJUK entered into appearance and contested the suit by filing written statement dated 28-3-2011 and better statement on 9-2-2015 stating that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, suit filed without giving statutory notice under the. Town Improvement Act, 1983 barred under estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and also under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The positive case of the defendant No.2, in brief, is that the suit property was allotted by. the DIT in favour of Hosn-erAra; that on 15-3-2005 she requested the RAJUK to attorn Ms. Nazma Khan as her constituted attorney in respect of her CWN (B) Plot No.28 Gulshan Residential Area; that it appears from the Memo issued by the Ministry of Housing and Works dated 22-10-2006 that said plot was released from the `kha' list of the abandoned property; that Nazma Khan filed some documents to transfer the said plot to Eastern Foods (Pvt.) Limited and claimed that it became owner as per Bainanama and power-of-attorney; that Nasir Khan, Managing Director of Eastern Food Ltd. informed the RAJUK that it became owner of the said plot through Bainanama and since Hosn-e-Ara failed to execute and register the said plot, it filed Title Suit No. 172 of 1999 and learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka passed status-quo order in respect of the suit plot; that on 25-3-2008 one Hosn-e-Ara filed an application to transfer of the suit plot with building in favour of MNH Bulu but the photo of Hosn-e-Ara did not tally with the photograph of Hosn-e-Ara in RAJUK file; that on 8-10-2001 RAJUK informed Hosn-e-Ara to put her signature and thumb impression before the law officer of the Ministry of Works and accordingly on 5-1 2001 she put her signature as directed. After that RAJUK asked Nazma Khan to file the original deed of power-of-attorney for comparing the signature of Hosn-e-Ara, but she did not file the said, deed in Rajuk; that further case of the defendant No. 2 is that RAJUK has got no knowledge in respect of the instant agreement neither any application nor any documents has been produced regarding the agreement alleged to be executed between the plaintiff and defendant No.1. That many other person have been seeking permission of the Said property by practicing fraud and Hosn-e-Ara preferred an application before the Ministry of Works on 21-8-2009 stating that somebody are trying to grab the suit property by creating false personation. So, without identifying the original Hosn-e-Ara, the plaintiff is not entitled to get any decree. With these averments the defendant No. 2 prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 8. Thereafter RAJUK filed better statement On 9-2-2015 stating the fact that So many persons are claiming the suit plot by showing them Hosn-e-Ara, who executed good number of Bainanama with several person and accordingly RAJUK as well as Ministry of works issued letters to the respective buyers to produce original lease agreement of Hosn-e-Ara in whose name the suit plot was leased out. Moreover, Title Suit No. 544 of 2009 has been filed in the Court of Second Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka by one Nazma Khan against Hosn-e-Ara and another. Title Suit No 423 of 2013 has been filed which is still pending. Thus the plaintiff is not entitled to get any relief before ascertaining the identity of the real lessee, Hosn-e-Ara. 

 10. 'That the case of defendant No. 3, in short, is that defendant No. 1, Hosn-e-Ara was the lessee of the suit property; that the said 'property was Wrongly appeared in the "Kha" list of the abandoned property list and defendant No. 1 in Order to release the suit property from the list filed a Settlement Case No. 360 of 1995 before the 1st Settlement Court, Dhaka and after taking evidence the said suit was allowed and the suit property was released from the 'kha’ list by judgment and order dated 29-6-1996; that thereafter; defendant No. 1 approached to sell the suit property to this defendant and this defendant agreed to purchase the same and accordingly an agreement for sale was registered on 21-8-1997 and Taka 35,00,000 was paid out of Taka 1,00,00,000 as earnest money and on the same date an Irrevocable Power of Attorney in respect of the suit was executed and registered in favour of Nazma Khan, Director of defendant No. 3 company and thereafter all the original documents in respect of the suit property was handed over to this defendant; that thereafter the Ministry of Housing and Works being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 20-6-1996 passed by the Settlement Court, filed a Writ Petition No.710 of 2002 before the Hon'ble High Court Division and the said power-of-attorney holder has taken necessary steps for disposal of the said writ petition. It is mentioned here that as per direction of the High Court Division the said Hosn-e-Ara physically appeared before the High Court Division with Domicile Certificate and after hearing the parties the Rule of the said writ petition was discharged by judgment and order dated 30-10-2002; that against which Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 637 of 2003 was filed by the Government before the Hon'ble Appellate Division, the said Civil Petition was also dismissed by order dated 16-4-2005 and the judgment passed by the settlement court was affirmed; that thereafter the said attorney tried her best to release the property from the list of the abandoned property but the authority did not pay heed to it and in lieu of that the said attorney filed Writ Petition No. 8512 of 2006 before the High Court Division for releasing the suit property from the list; that ultimately the said property was released from the abandon property list through gazette notification published on 6-9-2007; that thereafter defendant No. 1 filed an application to defendant No. 2 for accepting the irrevocable power-of-attorney which was made by defendant No. 1 in favour of Nazma Khan and defendant No. 2 accepted the same; that thereafter the said attorney filed an application to defendant No. 2 for fixing the transfer fee but as no response was made by defendant No. 2, she made a legal notice through her lawyer on 16-7-2008; that the lawyer of defendant No. 2 after proper scrutiny gave Opinion that there is no legal bar if the suit property is transferred by the attorney in favour of defendant No. 3. But as defendant No. 2 did not answer the legal notice, Writ Petition No. 5845 of 2008 was filed before the Hon'ble High Court Division, that said writ petition is still pending for hearing; that this defendant earlier filed Title Suit No. 172 of 1999 for specific performance of contract with the selfsame issue which is still pending before the Court of 1st Joint District Judge, Dhaka. That by practicing fraud, the plaintiff created the contract in question and Hosn-e-Ara appeared as defendant No. 1 is a fictitious person; that the Hosn-e-Ara in the written statement filed in Title Suit No. 5972 of 2008 which was continuing with the instant, suit analogous, specifically stated that she never entered into any contract with the plaintiff and the agreement in question is false; that the case of the Plaintiff is false and as such the suit is liable to dismissed. 

 11. The defendant No.1 and the plaintiff on 6-9-2015 filed joint application for compromise along with a fresh Vokalatnama without cancelling the earlier Vokalatnama filed by the same Advocate Mr Liakat Ali which was earlier canceled by the court by order dated 20-11-2006. That the terms of the said compromise petition is that contract in question that is the registered agreement No. 6359 dated 3-4-2006 is Valid one, defendant No.1 is entitled to get the rest amount of Taka 10 lac which can be withdrawn from the Court by the defendant No. 1 after registering the kabala and plaintiff is ready to pay Taka 5 lac in excess in favour of the defendant No. 1 and the application for compromise will do form part of the decree. In paragraph No.5 of the compromise petition it is categorically stated that: 

 15. It appears that in the present suit the trial court by order dated 21-10-2015, directed the plaintiff MNH Bulu, his attorney Anwarul Kabir the defendant No.1 Hosn-e-Ara to appear before the court personally. In the suit the added defendant No.3 filed three applications on 9-11- 2015; first one to cancel the solenama dated 6-9-2015, secondly one praying direction upon the defendant No.1 to submit the documents in respect of suit property and third one praying direction upon the plaintiff to submit the original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 which the plaintiff filed later on. But the trial court kept those application and passed order that same will be disposed of at the time of final hearing of the suit. The defendant No.3 again filed an application on 22-11-2015 under Order VII rule 11(d) read with Section 151 of the Code, of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint and that application was also kept with the record by order dated 11-1-2016 and next date was 'fixed on 25-1-2016 to produce evidence on behalf of RAJUK and other defendants. The defendant- No.3 filed an application for adjournment, on the other hand the defendant No.2 filed an application to recall DW-1 Tarikul Islam. After hearing, the prayer of defendant No.3 was rejected and directed to cross-examine DW-I. But the defendant No.3 did not take step and then next date was fixed for production the evidence on behalf of the defendant No.3. The defendant No.3 on 31-1- 2016 filed an application for adjournment on the ground that the, appellant already filed two revisional application before the .High Court against the order dated 11.1-2016 and 17-1-20016 but same was also kept with record. Later on by order dated 31-1-2016 the application for adjournment was rejected and the defendant No.3 was directed to produce evidence. The defendant No. 3 again on 2-2-2016 filed an application to cross-examine the witness of the plaintiff and to withdraw the suit form argument but it was rejected on 4-2-2016. The defendant No.3 filed an application to stay the further proceeding of the present suit till disposal his Transfer Miscellaneous Case No.69 of 2016 which was pending for hearing. After hearing the aforesaid application filed by the defendant No.3 was rejected by the trial court and passed the impugned judgment and decree dated. 4-2-2016. 

 19. He further submits that the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation on the ground that the present plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 429 of 2006 on 2-11-2006 in the First Court of Joint District Judge. Dhaka when the vendor of the Agreement, defendant No. 1 finally refused to execute and register the sale deed on 10-10-2006 and the instant suit was filed on 7-2-2008 showing die date that the plaintiff finally refused to execute registered sale deed on 23-10-2007. So, the present suit is clearly barred under the principle of res-judicata as well by limitation. He next submits that the Bainanama was registered on 3-4-2006 and the plaintiff offered the rest amount to the defendant No.1 on 23-10-2007 which is after 568 days and in pursuance of the said of agreement the contract has lost is force for not offering the rest amount within one year from the date of registration of the baina. But the court below completely over looking and in not considering this vital question. He also submits that the plaintiff in course of trial did not exhibit a single piece of document in support of his claim to prove his case in formal way. In this respect learned Advocate cited decisions reported in AIR 1928 Lahore 142. He further argued that the plaintiff the present suit for a decree of Specific Performance of Contract, in such suit the plaintiff should have prove the agreement by exhibiting the same and adducing evidence in support of document. But it is evident that the plaintiff failed to do so. He next submits that the present plaintiff has not come before the court with clean hand having regard to the fact that the present plaintiff against the same Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 earlier filed Title Suit No. 429 of 2006 for Specific Performance of Contract and the plaint of the said suit was rejected on the ground of non depositing of balance consideration money of Taka 10,000. But the plaintiff by suppressing the said fact filed the present suit although the present appellant tiled an application on 22-11-2015 under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the present plaint. He further submits that the present plaintiff earlier filed another Title Suit No. 398 of 2006 on 12-10-2006 for permanent injunction in respect of the same self property by impleading Hosn-e-Ara as defendant No.2. Hosn-e-Ara appeared and filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction. Thereafter another Hosn-e-Ara filed Vokalatnama through her engaged Advocate Mr Md. Liaquat Ali Sikder on 20-11-2006. Subsequently, on 29-11-2006 Vokalatnama filed Mr Md. Liaquat Ali Sikder, Advocate was cancelled as he failed to produce Hosn-e-Ara before the court. He also submits that the present title suit was taken up for analogous hearing with the Title Suit No. 398 of 2006 which was subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 5972 of 2008. But the learned Advocate for the defendant No.1 totally suppressing the fact of filing earlier Vokalatnama again filed a fresh Vokalatnama on behalf of defendant No.1 Hosn-e-Ara on 6-9-2015 and filed an application for compromise jointly with the plaintiff. 

 26. It may be noted that the defendant No.2 1 RAJUK filed documents by firisty dated 9-2-2015 and defendant No.3 also filed some documents with firstly when the defendant No.3 filed application under Order 1, rule 10 on 26-10-2009. Defendant No. 3 by second firisty dated 4-5-2015 further filed documents which includes Bainanama dated 21-8-1997 and plaint of Title Suit No. 172 of 1999 filed on 4-7-1999. In the suit plaintiff filed some documents by firisty dated 3-2016 to prove his case, the documents are, gazette notification dated 6-9-2007 for releasing the suit property from the `kha' list of the abandoned property, Certified Copy of the judgment dated 20-6-1996 passed by the First Court of Settlement, Dhaka releasing the suit property from the `kha' list of the abandoned property. Two letters dated 22-10-2006 and 19-10-2006 issued by Ministry of Housing and Works, judgment and order dated 30-10-2002 passed in Writ Petition No. 710 of 2002 discharging the Rule and upheld the judgment passed by the court of settlement, Order dated 16-4-2005 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 637 of 2003 filed by the government against the judgment and order dated 13-10-2002 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 710 of 2002 dismissing the leave petition as being time barred and photocopy of Allotment Letter dated 7-4-1962 and Lease Deed dated 22-9-1962 by DIT. 

 29. Let us now discuss and decide the issues Nos. 1 and 2. Firstly, it is the definite case of the plaintiff that the Bainanama was executed on 3-4-2006. On perusal of the record it is evident that at the time of filing of the present suit on 6-2-2008 the plaintiff filed only two documents, namely, photocopy of the certified copy of the Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 and original challan dated 6-2-2008 showing payment of balance consideration money of Taka 10 lac. It transpires that the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 filed separate written statement in the suit but defendant No.1 did not file any written statement in the suit. Upon consideration of the materials on record it appears that the defendant No.1 appeared in the suit by filing Vokalatnama through her learned advocate Mr Liaquat Ali but he failed to produce his client before the court then his Vokalatnama was cancelled by the court on 29-11-2006. But later on the defendant No. 1 filed fresh Vokalatnama on 6-9-2015 through his previous engaged Advocate and filed an application for compromise on same day jointly with the plaintiff. 

 34. On scrutiny of the case record, it appears that no list of exhibited documents were available in the record and the plaintiff to prove the case did not file the Original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006. It is apparent from the order sheet that the defendant No. 1 and plaintiff deposed on 6-9-2015 to prove the Solenama filed by the plaintiff and defendant No.1 but did not file the original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 on 6-9-2015 but the trial cowl decreed the suit on compromise on 4-2-2016 as per Solemnama dated 6-9-2015 and. accordingly decree was prepared on 11-2-2016. 35. Thus it is crystal clear that without filing the original Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 suit was compromised on 6-9-2015 but later on 9-11-2015 the original bainama was filed which is evident from Order No. 58 dated 9-11-2015 and surprisingly no documents including the original Bainanama was exhibited in the suit. Although there was a serious dispute with regard to the genuineness of the Bainanama and the signature appearing in the said Bainanama. So far execution of the Bainanama by the defendant No.1 in favour of the plaintiff, the defendant No.2 and defendant No.3 claimed that the said agreement was forged agreement created for the purpose of grabbing of suit land by the plaintiff. From the materials on record.it appears that although the defendant No.3 filed an application for verifying the signature of the defendant No.1 in the baina and to get expert opinion. 

 36. Section 107(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure has empowered the appellate court for a comparison by itself when necessary under Section 73 of the Evidence Act. In view of the said authority, we have examined and compared the signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the Bainanama dated 3-4-2006 with the admitted signature appearing in the documents mentioned namely—1) Vokalatnama filed by defendant No.1 in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008, 2) compromise petition dated 6-9-2015 filed by the plaintiff and defendant No.1, 3) deposition sheet of Hosn-e-Ara as DW I in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 dated 6-9-2015. 4) signature of the original lease agreement dated 22-9-1964 between DIT and Hosn-e-Ara and thumb impression appear therein, and 5) signature in mortgaged-deed dated 27-8-. 1970. between defendant No. 1 and The East Pakistan House Building Finance Corporation. After comparison, it is evident that the signature appearing in the above documents do not appear to be identical/similar with the signature appearing in the Bainanama in question dated 3-4-2006 (Exhibit-4) as such the case of the plaintiff regarding the Exhibit-4 is not proved. 

 37. It appears that at the time of filing of the compromise petition on 6-9-2015, the defendant No.1 filed fresh power again through his Advocate Liaquat Ali, whose power was cancelled earlier by the court on 29-11-2006 in Title Suit No. 398 of 2006, subsequently renumbered Title Suit No. 5972 of 2008 which will be heard analogously with present Title Suit No. 682 of 2008. It also appears that defendant No.3 filed an application in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 on 9-11-2015 praying for rejection of the compromise petition filed by the defendant No. l. but the learned Joint District Judge by order dated 9-11-2015 kept the same with the record stating that the same will be considered at the time of final adjudication of the suit. From those evidences is creates a series of doubt about the genuineness and bonafide of the agreement in question and inspired us to believe that the case of alleged contract on sale of the suit property and the case of reducing the contract into an agreement have been founded 'upon bundles of false hood. 

 40. This matter was heard by this Bench on good number of days and on the last three occasions Mr AKM Faiz, the learned Advocate appeared with Mr Shishir Kanti Majumder, Advocate for the respondent No.1 and when asked by this court, whether it will be possible on the part of the respondent No. 1 to produce Hosn-e-Ara before this court for proper adjudication and final settlement of the case. In reply, Mr AKM Faiz, learned Advocate on earlier two occasions submits that it will be possible to produce Hosn-e-Ara before This court after her return from Chennai, where she is now staying for her medical treatment. Since the respondent No. 1 took adjournments, accordingly the date of delivery of judgment was adjourned till 10-12-2018. On that date on the prayer of the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 delivery of the judgment of the appeal was deferred till today. Today (14-1-2019) Mr Shishir Karti Majumder, learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 without producing Hosn-e-Ara, submitted her original passport being No. 0442656 issued on 3-1-2019 along with a NID card being No. 2695-0469-48339 which was issued by the respective authorities on 29-4-2008 showing her address Holding No. 3/3(1) Chand Mia Housing, post Office Mohammadpur, 1207, Dhaka City Corporation and also filed photocopy of her earlier passport No. 095540 issued on 21-4-014. 

 41. In this connection it is very important to note that the trial court by Order No. 57 dated 21-10-2015 fixed Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 for hearing Joint compromise application filed by the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 and also for appearance of the original plaintiff, MNH Bulu. The defendant No. l submitted photocopy of her NID card and copy of passport those documents were be kept with the record. Plaintiff MNH Bulu his constituted attorney, Anowarul Kabir and defendant No.1 appeared in person in court and submitted their respective signature before the court and learned Joint District Judge passed order dispensing the personal appearance of plaintiff and defendant No.1 and prayer of defendant No.3 is allowed. But surprisingly enough those documents are not available in the case record. Moreover, plaintiff did not give any explanation why he appointed Anowarul Kabir as his constituted attorney. Later on 9-11-2015 plaintiff filed original Bainanama No. 6359 dated 3-4-2006 by filing firisty on that date. In the judgment the trial court failed to take notice of the fact that the plaintiff earlier filed Title Suit No. 429 of 2006 on 2-11-2006 for Specific Performance of Contract impleading the present defendant No.1, Hosn-e-Ara and defendant No.2 RAJUK as defendants. In the said suit present plaintiff showed last cause of action on 10-10-2006 but did not deposit balance consideration money of Taka 10 lac at the time of filing of the plaint, which is a pre-condition in filing the suit for Specific Performance of Contract for sale of any immovable property. Since the plaintiff did not file: the balance consideration money in accordance with the amended provision of Specific Relief Act, the trial court rejected the plaint as the suit is barred under Section 21A Sub-clause (b) of the Specific Relief Act. 

 42. It further appears that the plaintiff filed the present suit on 7-2-2008 showing the last cause of action on 23-10-2007 which is clearly barred by limitation under the principle of res-judicata. The trial court should have also considered that the Title Suit No. 398 of 2006 subsequently renumbered as 5972 of 2008 which was filed by the present plaintiff for permanent injunction. Later on, in the present suit learned Joint District Judge passed an order on 22-10-2008 that the present suit will be heard analogously with Title Suit No. 398 of 2006. Subsequently, on the prayer of the plaintiff Title Suit No. 5972 of 2016 was withdrawn by order dated 4-2-2016. 

 44. It further appears from the NID card of Hosn-e-Ara which was filed today before this court along with the original passport and photocopy of earlier passport the signature appearing in the NID card does not tally with the signature of Hosn-e-Ara Defendant No.1. In the NID card the signature of Hosn-e-Ara is in Bengali but the documents mentioned above the signature of Hosn- e-Ara appears in English. Further it is apparent from the Bainanama that the  address of the present defendant No. 1 is Plot No.28, House No. 119 Block-CWN(B) Gulshan Road, Dhaka but in the NID card filed in court today, her address was shown holding No. 3/3(1) Chand Mia Housing, Post Office Mohammadpur, 1207, Dhaka City Corporation. 

 48. In the result the appeal is allowed and the connected Rile being Civil Rule No. 119(F) of 2016 is disposed of. The judgment and decree dated 4-2-2016 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 682 of 2008 are set-aside. The suit is dismissed without any order as to costs.

full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J : This Civil Appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 6-1-2008 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in civil Revision No. 276 of 1998 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the judgment and decree dated 10-5-1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No.287 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Noakhali in Title suit No. 696 of 1974 dismissing the suit for declaration of title. 

 That the present respondent Nos.1-3 and two others instituted Title suit No. 696 of 1974 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) Noakhali, against the government and others for declaration of title in 10.26 acres' of land described in the schedule to the plaint. As the land of the appellants and others were included in the schedule to the plaint, they got themselves added as defendant Nos.5-11 in the suit on their application under Order I, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 4. The defendant No.1, defendant Nos.5-11 and 12-17 filed three sets of separate written statements to contest the suit. The defendant No.1 in its written statement stated inter (ilia that, the suit land was diluviated in 1344 BS and was under the water for more than 20 years. As a result the right, title and interest of Mohammad Hossain Miah or Hossain Ahamed Kazi was extinguished in consequence of the provisions of President Order No. 135 of 1972 and the same vested in Government without any encumbrance. During the last survey, the land was correctly recorded in the name of the Government. The S.A. record, prepared in the name of Mohammad Hossain Miah, the predecessor of defendants Nos. 2-4, was without any basis. The plaintiffs did not acquire any right, title or interest by the purchase deed from defendant Nos. 2-4 over the suit land as the said defendants had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The written statement filed by defendant Nos.5-11 and 12-17 are identical and, as such, the same does not require to be narrated elaborately. 

 5. In the written statement, fendant Nos. 5 to. 11 denied the entire plaint case of the plaintiffs. Their substantive cases are that Hossain Ahmed Kazi mortgaged 8 annas measuring 5.10 acres out of scheduled land of the plaint to Mohammad Hossain Miah which he redeemed. The suit land was diluviated from the possession of Hossain Ahmed Kazi, and government could not take possession as it was diluviated land at that time. After alleviation Hossain Ahmed Kazi took possession of the suit land. After the death of Hossain Ahmed Kazi his heirs added defendant Nos. 5 to 11 have been possessing the suit land by cultivating the same. It is stated that, the defendants denied the so called settlement of Mohammad Hossain Miah from government and they asserted that suit land was under water at the time of so-called auction by government. After alluvian, these defendants prayed for restoration of the holding in their names as the heirs of original owner and accordingly, the government restored the original holding in the name of these defendants vide restoration Miscellaneous Case No. 369 of 1972-73 and they paid dues and arrear rents to government. These defendants denied the right, title and interest of Mohammad Hossain Miah, his heirs and plaintiffs in the suit land and, as such, challenged the so-called deeds of the plaintiffs as claimed in the plaint. On the basis of the aforesaid assertion, the defendant Nos. 5 to 11 prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 7. In the written statement, defendant Nos. 12 to 17 asserted in the similar way as has been stated by the defendant Nos. 5 to 11 in their written statement and, as such, the same does not require to be stated again. In the written statement, the defendant Nos. 12 to 17 claim 2.25 acres out of the suit land as the heirs of the original owner, Hossain Ahmed Kazi and prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 8. The trial court, after hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31-8-1987. Against which the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 287 of 1987 before the learned District Judge, Noakhali. Subsequently, the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Noakhali who dismissed the same by his judgment and decree dated 10-5-1997. The plaintiffs then filed Civil Revision No.276 of 1998 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which ultimately has been made absolute by judgment and order dated 3-1-2008. 

 10. Mr. Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant appellant submits that the High Court Division committed error in making the Rule absolute without reversing the concurrent findings of both Courts below in as much as the plaintiffs could not prove their title and possession in the suit land, whereas the defendant proved the same. He submits that the High Court Division failed to consider the printed Kabuliyat dated 6-2-1937 (Exhibit 4) filed by the plaintiffs claiming that, to be the title document of their predecessor in its own perspective when on the face of the same it clearly appears to have been printed on 26-2-1954 from one Lucky Press, Chaumuhani, Noakhali and, as such, the basic document of the plaintiffs' predecessor being a false and ante dated document the same has not created any valid title of the plaintiffs or on their predecessor. Hence, all subsequent deeds filed by the plaintiffs having not created any legal right the same are forged and fabricated which has been rightly pointed out by the trial Court and affirmed by the Court of appeal below in its judgment. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that Mohammad Hossain Miah, predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendor, instituted Title Suit No. 70 of 1969 for declaration of his title for the self same land, but ultimately withdrew the same on 29-3-1974 without obtaining permission from the court to sue afresh and thus, filing of the instant suit by the plaintiffs in 1974 upon creating the alleged kabuliyat, the title deed of the predecessor of their vendors (defendants Nos. 2 to 4) suppressing the fact of filing and withdrawing the said suit clearly proves that they practiced fraud upon the Court which the Court of appeal, below rightly found that the instant suit is hit by Order XXIII, rule 3 of the Code. Mr. Chowdhury also submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as they did not pray for any consequential relief and also for non consideration of the material evidences on record. Lastly, he submits that the High Court Division made the Rule absolute against all the defendant opposite parties amongst whom defendant-opposite party Nos. 7, 8 and 13 died in the meantime during the pendency of .the Rule and, as such, the impugned judgment and order making the Rule absolute against the dead persons is a nullity. 

 11. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on Record appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 submits that both the Courts below without applying their judicial mind and upon non reading and misreading the materials on record came to an erroneous decision and thereby, dismissed the suit which the High Court Division upon full consideration of the materials on record set aside by the impugned judgment and order. According to him, PW 1 proved the Kabuliat submitted by the Government as Exhibit 4 showing that the plaintiffs got the settlement of the suit land from the Government, and they are possessing and enjoying the same without any hindrance. All the PWs, according to him, categorically proved the plaintiffs' possession in the suit land during the SA settlement and their names have been rightly prepared and published in the SA Khatian as Exhibit 1(ICa). He submits that the defendant No.1, the Government, claimed that the suit land was diluvion land which was under the water for long time and, as such, the plaintiffs' predecessor lost his title and possession over the suit land as no claim was ever made within the specific period. Such finding of the Courts below was totally misreading of materials on record inasmuch as had it been so the SA Khatian would never have been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He submits that no evidence has been led by the defendants to prove that the suit land was under water and, as such, the submissions of the defendants are totally wrong. He submits that the Courts below failed to consider that PW 1 proved the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) produced by the plaintiffs and also failed to consider and determine the possession of the plaintiffs although all the PWs categorically proved the same and the documents exhibited by the plaintiffs in support of their title and possession clearly proves their title and possession in the suit land by constructing houses and living there. Hence the findings of the courts below were erroneous. In support of his submission he relied on the case of Md. Nurul Islam vs Bangladesh, reported in 17 BLD (AD) 91 = 2 BLC (AD) 56; and thereby submitted that since construction of document is a mixed question of law and fact and the same having not properly been construed by the Courts below, the High Court Division was very much within its competence to reverse the said finding of fact arrived at by the Courts below giving cogent reason. He submits that the courts below failed to take into consideration Exhibit 1(Ka), S.A Khatian, Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) and the rent receipt (Exhibit 5) which obviously proved the plaintiffs' right, title and possession in the suit land. The High Court Division having considered those documents found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land and made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment. Lastly relying on the decision in the case of Hossain Ahmed Chowdhury vs Mr. Nurul Amin, reported in 47 DLR (AD) 162; Mr. Bhuiyan submits that when there is misreading of evidence and non consideration of some material evidence then it was incumbent on the revisional court to consider the same and to arrive at a proper finding on the material evidence on record and to finally dispose of the case. Thus the High Court Division has rightly made the Rule absolute which does not call for any interference by this Court. 

 12. From the facts and circumstances and the submissions of the learned advocates of both the sides as stated above, it appears that the whole crux of the case is the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) which is the title document of Mohammad Hossain Miah the predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendors. On perusal of the said Exhibit it appears that it has been printed from one "Lucky Press", Chaumuhani, Noakhali on 26-2-1954. From, the contents of the said exhibit it appears that the same has been executed on 6-2-1937 by the collector of Noakhali on behalf of the Governor of Bango Prodesh as one part and Mohammad Hossain Miah, predecessor of the plaintiffs' vendors as the other part and the same appears to have been given effect from 1344 BS in respect of 10.26 acres of land. After taking such settlement by the said Kabuliyat, the said Mohammad Hossain Mia died leaving behind defendants Nos. 2 to 4 as his heirs who, according to the plaintiffs, transferred the said land (suit land) to them. 

 13. It further appears that the trial Court on examination of the materials on record held that, only question for determination is whether the plaintiffs could prove that Mohammad Hossain Mia got the settlement through RS Case No. 650/36-37. On analyzing the materials on record it found that the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) has been executed on 6.2.1937 and has been accepted on 15-3-1950 and the form on which the said Kabuliat has been prepared appears to have been printed from one "Lucky Press", Chaumuhani, Noakhali on 26-2-1954 and thus the trial Court held that; how a Kabuliat claimed to have been executed on 6-2-1937 and accepted 15-3-1950 can be shown to have been executed in a form printed on 26-2-1954 from Lucky Press, Chaumuhani. It also held that the date of comparing the deed and printing of the Kabuliyat and the date of execution are not the same. Thus the Kabuliyat (Exhibit 4) is not a reliable document and no title and possession can be passed on the basis of such unacceptable document. From the materials on record the trial Court also found that the Government vide Certificate Case No. 201/33-34 auction purchased the suit land on 1-10-1936 which was confirmed on 4-12-1936 and RS Case No. 650/36-37 appears to have been filed and Kabuliyat appears to have been executed on 6-2-1937. So the chronology of dates also show that, after confirmation of auction sale within two months the RS case has been filed which clearly proves that within a year (actually two months) of getting the auction sale confirmed in favour of the Government, Mohammad Hossain Miah created the settlement by the said Kabuliyat. 

 15. Considering Exhibits 4 and 6 and the evidence on record the trial Court held that the claim of the plaintiffs that Mohammad Hossain Miah or his heirs, defendant Nos. 2 to 4 obtained right, title and possession in the suit land is not proved. All these findings have been affirmed by the court of appeal below who also held that Mohammad Miah, the predecessor of the defendants. Nos. 2 to 4 from whom the plaintiffs purchased the suit property also filed Title Suit No. 70 of 1969 against the Government on the same plea and the said suit was permitted to be withdrawn by Order No. 55 dated 23-3-1974 on payment of cost of Taka 15 to the defendant. The plaintiffs under such circumstances filed the instant suit without disclosing anything about filing of the earlier suit by Mohammad Hossain Miah and since there is no permission to sue afresh, the present suit filed by the plaintiffs claiming through the heirs of Mohammad Miah is hit by Order XXIII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thus the suit is not maintainable as filing of the subsequent suit, i.e. the instant suit on the self same cause of action, by the plaintiffs, is barred by law since the plaintiffs could not produce any paper that he took permission to sue afresh at the time of withdrawal of the earlier suit. 

 16. From the aforesaid facts and circumstances it is clear that Mohammad Hossain Miah and/or his heirs (defendants Nos. 2 to 4), the vendor of the plaintiffs had no title and possession in the suit land. Moreover it appears that the auction purchase of the government has been confirmed on 4-12-1936 and within two months of confirmation Mohammad Hossain Miah obtained Kabuliyat in his favour which is not at all practicable. Apart from this it also appears that Title Suit. No. 70 of 1.969 filed by Mohammad Hossain Miah against the government for declaration of his title in respect of the self same property has been withdrawn on 23-3-1974 of course without permission to sue afresh, and interestingly the plaintiffs claim that the defendants Nos. 2 to 4 have sold the same to them by four. Kabala deeds on 25-3-1974 i.e. within two days of such withdrawal of the earlier suit and immediately after purchase the plaintiffs instituted the present suit in 1974. Thus the whole transaction appears to be concocted on the basis of some forged documents. 

 17. Thus the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case and, as such, they are not entitled to get any relief and rather the defendants case that the suit land was under river for more than 20 (twenty) years and, as such, the title and possession has vested, in the Government, appears to be correct.
