full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.21 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession alleging, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff, Abdur Rahman, who while possessing the suit land, transferred the same to the defendant with a condition to redeem the same and delivered possession in his favour. But the defendant did not register the deed of re-conveyance in his favour, consequently he instituted Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 against him for redemption of the suit land and got a decree on 30.10.1968 and subsequently got the registration of the deed through Court. After the death of Abdur Rahman, the present plaintiff got delivery of possession of the land on 18.12.1980 through Court. The plaintiffs were living in other place, other than the suit land. In the month of February, 1981, the defendant forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land and as such, they filed the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter alia, that Abdur Rahman while owning and possessing the suit land sold .26 acre land to the defendant and his sister, Mosammat Ayesha Khatun alias Amena Khatun by a registered sale deed dated 03.08.1960. Subsequently, it was decided in a meeting to retransfer the said land, accordingly an agreement was executed on 03.08.1960 which was registered on the next date. Thereafter, Abdur Rahman filed Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 against him for specific performance of the said agreement, which was decreed on contest. Said Abdur Rahman thereafter brought Title Execution Case No.06 of 1972. During pendency of the execution case, said Abdur Rahman expressed his intention to sell the suit land including the structures thereon. On receipt of an agreed price, fixing taka 8,500.00, said Abdur Rahman executed and registered a deed on 19.08.1974 in the office of the Sub-Registrar, Mymensingh and since then defendant has been possessing the suit land. In the deed of sale, it was wrongly mentioned the year of the decree of the execution case as 1969 in place of 1972, but there has been inserted the exact number of such execution case. On the basis of that registered deed, the defendant got his name mutated and paid rent to the Government by opening separate Khatian bearing No.311. The alleged story of get-ting possession through the Court by the plaintiff and subsequently dispossessed by the defendant are all false and fabricated and accordingly, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court framed 8(eight) issues for the purpose of determination of the real controversy and consideration of case and considering the evidence on record along with documents, decreed the suit declaring the plaintiffs title over the suit land and also awarding a decree of recovery of khas possession by the judgment and decree dated 17.05.1993. 

 "Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Senior Advocate, submits that the learned Judge of the High Court Division travelled beyond the pleadings and the evidence on record and recorded finding that the Courts below committed error in cancelling the deed of the defendants as there was no question raised against the defendants deed exhibit-`G' not any issue was framed nor the defendants were given any opportunity to prove their documents and the observation were all made surmises and conjecture based on misconception of law. The learned Counsel further submits that the concurrent finding of facts of the Courts below regarding defendants sale deed dated 17.12.1974 which was made long before the acquisition of title by defendants vendor, the plaintiff on 17.03.1976 by sale deed executed and registered through Court in execution of a decree for specific performance of contract and got possession thereof on 18.12.1980 and that the defendants title deed dated 17.12.1980 and that the defendants title deed dated 17.12.1974, being a forged document, and thus, the same being void abnitio does require at by the High Court Division "Unless and until and defendants deed, is cancelled in a property constituted suit, the title and possession of the defendants cannot be said to be illegal and unauthorized" is erroneous. The learned Counsel next submits that a suit for specific performance of contract against the defendants were filed, which was decreed and in execution of the said decree the plaintiffs obtained a kabala and the possession of the claim of defendants that the said decree is not binding on them is completely false and concocted and lastly Mr. Quayum submits that in view of the concurrent findings of the Courts below relying upon and believing the documents exhibit-2 as well the depositions of PWs 3 and 4 the finding of the High Court Division that as the process server could not state the alleged date of delivery of possession, inference cannot be drawn up from exhibit-2 that the plaintiff got delivery of possession through Court on 18.12.1982, is misconceived and misleading." 

 8. Mr. AKM Jaglul Haider Afric, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the High Court Division finds that the Courts below have committed mistake in cancelling the defendant's deed (exhibit-Thha'). He further submits that the defendant had acquired title the suit land vide his alleged title deed dated 17.12.1974 (exhibit-Thha') prior to his vendor who acquired the same vide a sale deed executed on 15.03.1976 and registered on 17.03.1976 (exhibit-1) through Court in execution of the decree and they also got delivery of possession on 18.12.1980 through exhibit-'2' and as such, the High Court Division ought to have considered that the defendant's deed in question being out and out forged and void abinitio does not require to be cancelled and in that view of the matter, the findings of the High Court Division that "unless and until the defendant's deed is cancelled, his title and possession cannot be said to be illegal" is mis-conceived and cannot sustain in law. He further submits that the defendant having not executed and registered the deed of re-conveyance in favour of the plaintiff in terms of the Court's decree as well as the plaintiff having got the deed executed and registered and delivery of possession of the suit land through Court in execution of the decree as aforesaid the defendant's alleged claim of satisfying the decree is nothing but a false, fraudulent and concocted plea to frustrate the Court's decree and grab the suit land. He further submits that in view of the concurred findings of the Courts below made relying upon and believing the Court's document (exhibit-2) as well as the depositions of PWs 3 and 4, the very findings of the High Court Division that "as the process server could not say the exact date of delivery of possession is also misconceived." 

 11. It is admitted by the parties that one Abdur Rahman was the owner in possession of the disputed land who obtained a decree of re-conveyance in Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966 on 30.10.1968. The appellants as plaintiffs have come with an allegation that they acquired the title of the suit land by way of inheritance from aforementioned Abdur Rahman as his heir who duly got delivery of possession of such land on 18.12.1980 through Court in execution of aforesaid decree, but in the month of February, 1981, the defendant-respondent dispossessed them from the suit land forcibly. 

 13. The learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants strenuously argued that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiff-appellants acquired the right, title and interest over the suit land by dint of decree of re-conveyance and obtained possession through Court in execution of such decree and as such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division ought to have held that the alleged deed of the defendant in question is out and out false, forged and concocted but instead of doing so, the learned Judge of the High Court Division reversed the concurrent finding of the Courts below which is not sustainable in law. 

 14. On the other hand, Mr. Mahbubey Alam, leaned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondents controverted the aforesaid argument of the plaintiff-appellants and counter argued that though the suit being Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966, it had been established that the kabala dated 13.04.1960 in favour of the predecessor of the defendant-respondents was a mortgage deed and not out and out sale deed and the Court of first instance on the basis of such observation directed this defendant to re-convey the suit land in favour of Abdur Rahman. He also argued that the present defendant-respondents instead of challenging such order in an appellate forum, he has waived his claim of out and out sale and abode by such order of the Court and as a result of which, aforesaid Abdur Rahman acquired absolute right and title over the land in dispute and thereafter, the defendant-respondents again purchased the suit land by kabala dated 19.08.1974 at a consideration of taka 8500.00 from said Abdur Rahman. The learned Senior Advocate further argued that there is no anomaly or irregularity or illegality in such purchase which has been held before execution of the decree passed in Other Class Suit No.144 of 1966. Over and above, he argued that the plaintiff-appellants failed to prove the facts of aforementioned execution since the process server failed to disclose the date of delivery of possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff-appellants. 

 16. The defendant while deposing as PW 1 stated that after pronouncement of judgment, the plaintiffs' side filed an execution case and thereafter, he approached Abdur Rahman to sell the suit land again to him and at one point of time, he agreed to sell the same at a consideration of taka 8500.00 and accordingly, Abdur Rahman executed a sale deed on 19.08.19 14 on receiving consideration money. The defendant-respondents filed the original kabala dated 19.08.1974 before the trial Court which has been marked as exhibit-'Chha'. He further deposed that in the recital of such kabala, it has been stipulated that Abdur Rahman has sold out the subsisting interest of the suit land after being satisfied regarding the execution case of the decree passed in Other Class Case No.144 of 1966. He also deposed that he has been possessing the suit land since 1960 from the date of his first purchase on mutating his name in suit khatian and thereafter erected pucca structure therein after obtaining plan from the municipality and the fact of dispossession dated 26.02.1981 is false and concocted story. He also deposed that in this regard, he has filed an information slip issued by the Court (exhibit-'G') from which it is seen that there is no date of delivery in the execution register and as such, the writ of delivery of possession has been created for the purpose of this case with a view to defeat the right of the defendant-respondent. 

 18. The aforementioned recital of the deed has been corroborated by the testimony of DW3, Abdul Matin, a man of 73 years who has a shop by the side of this suit land. DW3, Abdul Matin deposed that Abdur Rahman settled to sell the suit land in favour of Abul Hashem at consideration of taka 8500.00 and talk of such settlement was held in his shop in between the parties and he was present there as well as in the Sub-Registrar's office on 19.08.1974 and the payment was made in his presence. He also deposed that Abdur Rahman executed the deed in his presence and he identified the signature which has been marked as exhibit-2(2). Having considered the aforementioned testimonies of DWs 1 and 3 along with the recital of the deed dated 19.08.1974, we have no hesitation to hold that the defendant has been able to prove that the existence of such kabala dated 19.08.1974 on adducing proper evidence. We also hold the view that during continuance of the execution proceeding of Title Execution Case No.06 of 1969 both the parties agreed to sell the suit land and again in favour of the defendant-respondent and accordingly kabala dated 19.08.1974 has been registered. 

 23. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division after proper appreciation of facts and circumstances arrived at a decision that the plaintiffs failed to prove the facts of getting delivery of possession through Court as well as the date of dispossession by the defendants. It has been further held that since the defendants found to have obtained title of the suit land by way of registered sale deed dated 17.12.1974 from the original owner, Abdur Rahman and remained in possession thereof, unless and until the said deed is cancelled in a proper suit, the title and possession of the defendants cannot be said to be illegal and unauthorized and as such, the suit must fail.

parties:
Afiluddin Sheikh being dead his heirs: Md. Abdul Latif and others ---- Appellants

-Vs-

Asan Sardar being dead his heirs Md. Hamjer Sarder and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case, in short, arc that the appellants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.109 of 1986 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Kushtia for declaration of title of the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Aduri Nesa who sold the same to the plaintiff by a registered sale deed in year, 1960. The plaintiff as an owner by purchase has been possessing the suit land for more than 12 years. But on 16.09.1985, the defendants for the first time claimed their title in respect of the suit land; hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos.1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter alia, that Aduri Nesa, mother of the defendants was original owner of the suit land. After her death, the defendants inherited the land. The plaintiffs were the Borgaders under Aduri Nesa and used to cultivate the suit land. After the death of Aduri Nesa, the defendants refused to make any new borga contract with the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs manufactured the alleged kabala deed dated 11.04.1960 executed by Aduri Nesa by false personification. The kabala dated 11.04.1960 is forged, collusive and not binding upon the defendants. The suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.293 of 1998 before the District Judge, Kushtia and on transfer, the appeal was heard and disposed of by the then Subordinate Judge, Kushtia who by the judgment and decree dated 19.11.1992 allowed the appeal setting aside those of the trial Court. 

 9. Mr. ASM Khalekuzzaman, learned. Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that it was written in the schedule to the sale deed dated 11.04.1960 that in total 1.95 acres land were sold but inadvertently it was written in words "one acre fifty-six decimals of land" and the High Court Division wrongly declared that since the plaintiffs have established their right, title and interest in respect of 1.56 acres land pursuant to the deed, exhibit 4 and disposed of the Rule with observation that the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. He further submits that in the deed and in the schedule to the sale deed dated 11.04.1960, it was written arithmetically in three places that the land sold was 1.95 acres mentioning the total rent of taka 611/7 pai but in words it was wrongly written in one place that one acre and fifty six decimals of land were sold and the High Court Division ought to have believed that total 1.95 acres land were sold out but without considering these aspects illegally disposed of the Rule with observation that the impugned judgment and order is bad in law and the same is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Mr. N. K. Saha, Senior Advocate, appearing for respondent No.1 submits that the appellate Court below being the last Court of fact, after consideration of the evidence on record, opined that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case, the said finding the appellate Court cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction. He further submits that the deed by which the plaintiffs claimed their right is not genuine and the appellate Court found that one of the stamp amounting to taka 30.00 during the British Regime of British origin but there is no assertion in the said deed that during the regime of Pakistan period, it was valid or not. He further adds that even in the said stamp, some over writings having been found and both the Courts below opined that the date of purchase was mentioned as 07.07.1969 and that the trial Court opined that it was corrected without any initial of the concerned officer which is a simple mistake, but it can-not be considered that a mere mistake of the officer concerned makes the document forged and concocted document. He further submits that since the appellate Court after consideration of the evidence on record opined that the impugned deed is not genuine which is a finding of fact; the said finding of fact of the appellate Court cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. He submits that though the concerned officer proved the said deed but he categorically stated that in the balam book, it is found to be 1.56 acres land whereas the trial Court erroneously passed the decree for entire 1.95 acres land. He further submits that the plaintiffs did not make any specification of the suit land and the suit for declaration of title is not maintainable in an unspecified land. He further submits that though as per evidence of PW7, the plaintiffs can get only 1.56 acres land, without any prayer for partition on Court can pass a decree in an unspecified land and that in such circumstances, the Rule ought to have been discharged. He further submits that by now the settled principle of the law in exercising the revisional power under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure has been laid down in several judicial pro-nouncement of the Appellate Division of the Court the finding of facts whether con-current or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court is final unless it is manifestly perverse and that in this connection reliance can be made on the decision in the case of Khurshed Ali and others-Vs-Noorjahan Bewa and others reported in 15 BLD (AD) 82 wherein it has been held:-"When the Appellate Court as the final Court of fact decides question of fact and records it findings of consideration of the evidence on record, the High Court Division while exercising revisional jurisdiction cannot interfere with the finding of facts unless the High Court Division is satisfied that the findings are perverse when the materials finding of the Appellate Court are upheld by the High Court Division and in doing so it commits no error of law, the decision of the High Court Division call for no interference. In the present case there is no finding that the finding of the appellate Court is perverse." He further submits that another decision can also cited in the case of Hazari Bala Sana and others-Vs-Niron alias Niranjan Mondol and others reported in 17 BLD (AD) 295 wherein it has been stated "It is a settled principle that the finding of facts, whether concurrent or not, arrived at by the lower Appellate Court, which is the final Court of fact, is binding on the High Court Division, as a revisional Court, Except in certain well defined exceptional circumstances, such as non-consideration or misreading of the material evidence affecting the merit of the case." He further submits that unless there is perversity in the finding due to non-consideration or misreading of material evidence occasioning failure of justice the findings of fact arrived at by the Court of appeal below on proper appreciation of evidence, cannot be interfered with by the High Court Division in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. 

 12. Admittedly, the suit land originally belongs to one Aduri Nesa and S.A record was prepared in her name. The appellants (plaintiffs) claimed to have purchased such land from Aduri Nesa by kabala dated 11.04.1960 and since then they have been possessing the same peacefully for more than 12 years. 

 "Once such a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody section 30 of the Evidence Act entitles the Court to presume that it is a genuine document." 

 25. Now the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendants assailed the kabala dated 11.04.1960 on two counts. (1) The plaintiffs have created the kabala dated 11.04.1960 by means of forgery using the stamp of paper amount to taka 30/- of British origin having no explanation as to whether the same was valid till the time of registration which was allowed to continue then Pakistan resume. (2) The quantum of land sold in such kabala dated 11.04.1960 is 1.56 and not of 1.95 acres land and also that actually the plaintiffs purchased only 1.56 acres land instead of 1.95 acres and in that case 1.56 acres land has no demarcation or specification with a view to make the suit land identifiable and as such, the suit for simple declaration is not maintainable without any prayer for partition as has been held by the revisional Court. 

 28. The appellate Court below on this count has arrived at a decision that there is no reason to believe that long after thirteen year of independence, the stamp paper of British origin was valid in Pakistan although there was a seal and Sub-Treasurer, Chuadanga who has put his signature on the stamp paper. The appellate Court below farther hold that there are over writing on the back page of the stamp and on perusal of the entire circumstances it appears to him that the deed in question was illegally created and fabricated one by means of forgery but the trial Court erroneously arrived at a wrong decision that there is no illegality in presenting and registering kabala in question since British Indian Stamp Paper was allowed to use till and after the date of registration.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.4154 of 2017
parties:
Md. Salim Sarder being dead his legal heirs: Most Monira Sultana and another. ------- Petitioners
-Vs-
Md. Abul Kashem and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the present petitioners as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.98 of 1996 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Court No.2, Rajshahi for declaration that the plaintiffs had title over the suit property as described in schedule-A to the plaint by way of adverse possession. By subsequent amendment of the plaint, another prayer was inserted to the effect that a decree may be passed that the deed of exchange bearing No. 718 dated 03.01.1975 executed and registered in Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/ 1972-1973 in favour of the defendant as described in schedule-B to the plaint is false, baseless, forged, ante-dated and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 3. The case as has been described in the plaint, in short, is that the suit lands appertaining to S.A Khatian No.142 originally belonged to one, Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh in equal share and the S.A. record was accordingly prepared and published in their names. While enjoying title and possession over the said property, they exchanged the same with those of the Indian property belonged to one Layebuddin Sarkar and accordingly, a deed of exchange was registered in between the parties on 27.01.1964. While Layebuddin Sarkar was enjoying title and possession over the properties, he sold out the same to one Habibur Rahman, predecessor of the plaintiffs at a consideration of taka 10,000.00 and executed a deed of sale on 03.04.1967, but due to time constrained, the same could not be registered on that very date, but it was agreed that the said deed would be presented for registration on the following day, but it could not be registered on the following day as Layebuddin Sarkar had to go to India and eventually, for his not coming back, the said deed remained unregistered. 

 4. Though the said deed was not registered, the recipient of it, Habibur Rahman, got possession of the suit properties on 04.04.1967 and continued to possess the same. However, during enjoyment of title and possession over the suit properties, Habibur Rahman died on 29.09.1979 leaving behind 4(four) sons and 5(five) daughters, the plaintiffs as his legal heirs who have been possessing the suit property to the hostile of the title of the defendants for more than 12 years since 04.04.1967 and as such, the plaintiffs have acquired title by way of adverse possession. It has further been stated that the defendants have got no right, title and possession over the suit properties. They by virtue of some false and concocted documents denied the title of the plaintiffs in the suit properties on 17.11.1986 and hence the suit. 

 6. Defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that, one Kanai Lal Ghosh executed a deed of exchange with the present defendant of his Indian property and accordingly, a power of attorney was executed and to revalidate the said deed of exchange, the defendant presented the said deed of exchange before the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi and thus, Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/1972- 1973 was started and after investigation, the deed of exchange was found to be genuine basing on which the Deputy Commission validated 6.20 acres land including the suit land by registered deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975. It has further been stated in the written statement that, in the event of enlisting the suit properties as vested and non-resident property in R.S record in the name of the Government, this defendant filed an application for releasing the same from the list and the Government released the said property on 20.10.1983. Upon releasing the said property, the defendant then mutated his name and accordingly paid rent to the Government. It has further been stated that, during enjoyment of title and possession over the said property, defendant No.1 transferred 8.14 decimals land to defendant No.2 on 25.11.1986 as well as some portion of land to defendant No.3 on 18.12.1986 and the said recipients have also been in possession over the same. In aforesaid manner, the defendants acquired title and possession over the suit land by adverse possession and the suit so filed by the plaintiffs has no basis which is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Defendant Nos.2-3 contested the said suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending that they purchased the suit properties from defendant No.1 dated 25.11.1986 as well as 18.12.1986 and since then, they have been enjoying title and possession over the suit property. After purchase, these two defendants also mutated their names and paid rent, so they prayed for dismissing the suit. 

 10. Challenging the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiffs then preferred Title Appeal No.165 of 1998 before the District Judge, Rajshahi. The said appeal was subsequently heard by the learned Judge, Jananirapatta Bingnokari Oporadh Daman Tribunal and Special Judge No.2, Rajshahi. 

 13. Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that their predecessor, Layebuddin Sarker, got the suit proper-ties by way of deed of exchange dated 27.01.1964 executed in Murshidabad, India with the properties of Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh located in Bangladesh and by virtue of the said deed of exchange, Layebuddin Sarkar transferred the same to the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Habibur Rahman on 03.04.1967 and since then, the plaintiffs have been enjoying title and possession over the suit land uninterruptedly within the every knowledge of the defendants and thereby the plaintiffs acquired title by adverse possession and the said deed dated 03.04.1967 has correctly been marked as exhibit No. 1. He further submits that the very deed dated 03.04.1967 has subsequently been acted upon by virtue of the deed dated 12.11.1990 through which the plaintiffs transferred an area of 10 decimals land to a school who was made co-plaintiff No.8 to the suit and the Headmaster of the school deposed as PW8 to prove the transfer of the suit land in their favour which has alternatively proves that the plaintiffs by virtue of the said deed acquired indefeasible title over the suit properties. He further submits that though defendant No.1 claimed to have acquired the suit properties by way of deed of exchange dated 18.01.1965 executed and registered in Murshidabad, India marked as exhibit No.2, but the same was out and out a sale deed and not a deed of exchange and the plaintiffs by collecting the said deed as well as other documents related to the said deed has been able to prove that defendant No.1 never executed any deed of exchange in India which alternatively proves that the plaintiffs have got title and possession in the suit properties. He further submits that in order to prove the execution of their deed dated 03.04.1967 as genuine, the plaintiffs adduced PW2 who is the attested witness of the said deed and the said PW2 has very perfectly proved the execution of the said deed without any deviation in his cross-examination by defendant No.1. He further submits that since the defendant's alleged deed of exchange dated 18.01.1965 has been proved to be false, the subsequent deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975 executed and registered by the Deputy Commissioner in favour of defendant No.1 has also been proved to be vague and collusive. He lastly submits that the deed dated 03.04.1967, date has been mentioned on the upper side of the stamp paper on which the said deed was written and also pointed out that since the stamp paper had been purchased in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs, so there has been no ambiguity with regard to the execution of the said deed as the said deed was also marked as exhibit even without any objection on the part of the defendants. 

 14. Mr. M. Amirul Islam, learned Counsel, who entered caveat on behalf of respondent No.1, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He further submits that though the plaintiffs claimed title over the suit property by way of adverse possession, but they have utterly failed to prove so by any convincing evidence while the defendants have produced rent receipt which was marked as exhibit-'Ghat series which aptly proves that the defendants have possession in the suit properties. He further submits that in order to validate a deed of exchange by any persons who are not the national of this country has to show and prove power of attorney supposed to be given by the person who belonged to the land in this country and by virtue of which, the Government used to validate such deed of exchange and in compliance so, the deed of exchange executed in favour of defendant No.1 was validated by the Government on 03.01.1975 which was marked as exhibit. But on the contrary, though the plaintiff claimed to have a deed of exchange from Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh by their predecessor, Habibur Rahman, but not a scrap of paper of such sort has ever produced by the plaintiff which clearly implies that the plaintiffs have utterly failed to show the basis of acquiring title in the suit land. He further submits that in order to establish title by way of adverse possession, the claim has to be made against the real owner in assertion of their hostile title and denying the title of the real owner. But in the instant case, the plaintiff though claimed title against the defendants, they did not admit defendant No.1 as the real owner in the suit land and without admitting said defendant No.1 as the real owner in the suit property, the suit could not be maintained. He further submits that the title in favour of the defendants has rightly been accrued and acted upon in view of subsequent transfer of near about 17 decimals land to defendant Nos.2-3 which clearly proves that having been acquired right, title and possession over the suit proper-ties, the defendants transferred the suit properties on acquiring title by virtue of the deed of exchange dated 03.01.1975. He further submits that though the plain-tiffs based their title over the suit proper-ties by virtue of sale deed dated 03.04.1967, there has been no mention of any date in the alleged deed, neither in the schedule nor in the body of the said deed. In that regard, he candidly submits that since there has been no date basing on the said, no title can be passed in favour of the plaintiffs and that there being no merit in the leave petition, the same is liable to be dismissed. 

 16. On the other hand, the respondents as defendants counter-claimed inter-alia that original owner, Kanai Lal Ghosh and Moniram Ghosh executed a deed of exchange which was duly validated by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi through Exchange Case No.134/Sadar/ 1972-1973. It has been further alleged that the defendant-respondents duly released the suit property from the list of vested and non-resident property and got the same mutated in their names and also have been possessing the same on payment of rent to the Government. It has further been claimed that during the period of such enjoyment, defendant No.1 transferred 8.14 acres lands to defendant No.2 on 25.11.1986 as well as some portion of land to defendant No.3 on 18.12.1986 who used to possess the aforesaid property and as such, they prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 18. On the other hand, the petitioners' claim is based on an unregistered sale deed which does not confer any title to the recipient of such deed as per provision of sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act. The petitioners' further claim is that they have been inducted into possession in 1967 and being in such possession, they have acquired statutory title by way of adverse possession and as such, the petitioners are entitled to get a decree for such statutory right. The defendant-respondents have vehemently opposed such statement of uninterrupted 'possession on adducing three DWs including defendant No.1, Abul Kashem. At this stage, it is impossible to taste the veracity of those wit-nesses, but it can be safely concluded that title follows possession. Over and above, it reveals from the record that La.yebuddin, alleged vendor of the plaintiff had to go to India frequently even on the date of registration of deed. Thus, the uninterrupted possession as alleged by the plaintiff is not at all believable. Apart from that, the act of hostility in support of their adverse possession is absent in this case which is very much essential with a view to acquire such statutory title. It is a bonafide proposition that in order to obtain a statutory title by way of adverse possession, the possession is to be not only openly but also hostily, notoriously runs against the true owner beyond statutory period of limitation and also that apparent show of exclusive possession is not sufficient of defeat the title of the real owner. The evidence from the plaintiffs (petitioners) side is totally lacking for establishing the fact that from a particular point of time, they started to possess the suit land asserting their title by adverse possession denying that title of the real owner to their knowledge as well as to the knowledge of the others as has been held by their lordships in the case of Shaik Farik-Vs-Abdul Wadud Sikder reported in 58 DLR (AD) 2006 page 248. 

 19. It reveals from exhibit-Thha' filed by the defendant that on 19.12.1987, one Selim Sarder, Abu Sarder, Anower Sarder and Shamsur Sarder who are none but the sons of plaintiff No.1 filed this petition before the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi for allotting the suit land in their favour stating that they have been possessing the suit land for some years (কয়েক বছর). If that very assertion is taken to be true, then the very assertion of the plaintiff that they have been enjoying title and possession for more than 30 years proves to be totally untrue. Thus, it appears that no adverse possession by way of statutory title has been accrued in favour of the plaintiff. 

 20. On perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division, it appears that the learned Single Judge came to the conclusion that the judgment of the Appellate Court was not a proper judgment of reversal. In coming to this conclusion, the said Court noticed that the trial Court had considered the material evidence in detail in coming to its finding of title and possession in favour of the plaintiffs, but the Appellate Court without discussing the evidence had abruptly reversed the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court on holding that the petitioners have acquired statutory title on the basis of their possession which is not sufficient to detect the title of real owner. We find no error of law in the view taken by the High Court Division.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Md. Anwar Hossain and others. ------ Appellants
-Vs-
Mosammat Hoshneara Begum alias: Putul being dead her heirs: Kamrul Islam and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The respondents instituted the original suit as plaintiffs for declaration of title to the suit land in the schedule of the plant and subsequently by amendment of the plaint also prayed for recovery of khas possession on alleging that the land measuring 19½ decimals appertaining to mouza-Bagura Alekanda in J.L. No.50 under C.S. Khatian Nos.160 and 178, Plot No.1548 belonged to Gobinda Shil: He executed a will and appointed his wife-Sona Lakhsmi as executrix. Defendant No.3, Ramesh Chandra Shil, was the next reversioner. After the death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, Sona Lakhsmi filed Probate Case No.6 of 1917 before the District Judge, Barisal. Sona Lakhsmi and the reversionar heir leased out the said land to Dinabandhu Gangopadhya (father of defendant Nos.1 and 2) by patta dated 05.11.1941 for legal necessity and delivered possession thereof. In the said patta by mistake Plot No.1549 was written instead of Plot No.1548, but the boundary and the area of the land were correctly written. Since the said pattan, defendant Nos.1 and 2 had been residing on the suit land by constructing dwelling structures thereon on payment of rent, municipal tax etc. The said defendants transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by registered sale deed dated 12.05.1970, but in that sale deed also mistakenly Plot No.1549 was written in lieu of Plot No.1548. During R.S. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother-Sona Lakhsmi although they had never claimed the same. Husband of defendant No.6 in collusion with Sudhir Chandra Dutta, an employee of defendant No.5, constructed structures on Plot No.804, and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'lcha' scheduled land. The collusively pre-pared wrong record in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother has clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No.6 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the plaint case contending, inter alia, that Sona Lakhshmi Shil and her next reversioner did not execute and register the alleged patta dated 05.11.1941 in favour of defendant Nos. l and 2 and no such patta was acted upon. Dinobundhu Gangopadhya or his heirs, defendant Nos.l and 2 never possessed the suit land. The land of CS Plot No.1549 has been recorded in RS Plot Nos.798-803/2001-2004. Manindra and others owned the suit land in Mirash ejara right. Plot No.1548 was possessed by temporary lessees of Sona Lakhshmi, named Bipin Behari, Abdul Aziz, Hiron Kumar Karmakar and three other persons. Defendant No.5 attempted to acquire the land of temporary tenant, Abdul Aziz. When landlord Ramesh Chandra Shil attempted to make the land khas, defendant No.5 took settlement on 29.12.1945 in Mirash ejara right of the land of Plot No.1548 and as he failed to get khas possession of the entire property, he gradually purchased the interests of temporary tenants and obtained khas possession of the suit land. Defendant No.5 made constructions in the suit land, opened municipal holding and mutated the property in his name and in the name of his wife and inducted tenants therein on monthly rental basis. Defendant No.5 and his wife transferred 0.431 acre land including the suit land to defendant No.6 by a registered sale deed dated 01.09.1969 at a consideration of taka 6,000.00. After purchase, defendant No.6 mutated her name in the revenue records and in the municipality in respect of the land and constructing structures thereon, she has been possessing some part of the suit land herself along with the members of her family and some parts through the monthly tenants. The plaintiffs have no title, interest and possession in the suit land, and they have filed the suit to grab the same creation forged maner and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 4. On conclusion of hearing of the suit, the trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 11.06.1990 dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff's preferred Title Appeal No.157 of 1990 before the District Judge, Barisal. The learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Barisal who heard the appeal, by his judgment and decree dated 06.10.1994 dismissed the same affirming those of the trial Court. 

 "Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners has contended that both the Courts below on consideration of the evidence on record oral and documentary having concurrently found. That the plaintiffs failed to establish their right, title, interest in the C.S. plot No.1548, the learned judge of the High Court Division committed error of law in sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court with a direction to dispose of the same after "investigation of the suit land by appointing another Advocate Commissioner" to ascertain the suit land invoking the inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Islam has further contended that the order of remand passed by the learned Judge of the High Division is against the well settled principle that order of remand cannot be made to afford opportunity to an unsuccessful party to fill up the lacuna in evidence. Mr. Islam has further contended that there being concurrent finding to the effect that it is the contesting defendant who is in possession of the suit land and the plaintiffs are in possession in the adjacent land the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and order in sending the suit back on remand with the purpose to ascertain the suit land. Mr. Islam has lastly con-tended that it being a well settled legal proposition that inherent power cannot be invoked while acting under specific provisions of law, the le9rned Judge of eh High Court Division acted beyond the scope of revision in giving direction upon the trial Court to dispose of the suit after holding local investigation of eh suit land invoking the inherent power. On the above submissions Mr. Islam prays for granting leave to appeal by this Court." 

 17. On the other hand, Ext. Jha(1) shows that the defendants and their predecessor duly mutated their names in suit khatian and have been paying rent to the government through dakhilas (Ext ‘cha’-series). SA and RS records of right have been prepared in the names of the defendant-appellants and their predecessors. Those records of right, mutation, rent receipts, tax receipt in respect of suit land are the evidence of possession, yet title follows possession. Particularly, RS record has been prepared after holding local survey and on ascertaining the existing possession. Thus, the fact of possession and dispossession as has been alleged by the plaintiffs (respondents) is not at all believable which appears to be negated the plaintiffs' prayer for khas possession. 

 18. Having considered those fact, circumstances and evidence on record, it appears that the trial Court as well as the Appellate Court below being the last Court of fact has rightly appreciated those evidence on record and came to a conclusion concurrently that the plaintiff(respondents) failed to prove the fact of creation of any such alleged tenancy right in favour of Dinabandhu Gangopadhya under land-lord-Sona Lakhsmi and others and also failed to establish their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. We find that there is no misreading, non-consideration and mis-appreciation in the concur-rent findings of the learned Judges of the trial Court and the Appellate Court below. 

 19. In spite of that the learned Judge of the High Court Division travelled beyond the scope of the revision in making the Rule absolute and sending the suit back on remand to the trial Court for hearing afresh although both the Courts of fact have arrived at a concurrent finding of fact that the plaintiffs (respondents) have failed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in RS Plot No.1548 tracing back their title therein through the patta dated 05.11.1941. 

 22. We also find that inherent power cannot be invoked while acting under specific provisions of law, the learned Judge of the High Court Division acted beyond the scope of the revision without averting the concurrent finding on title and possession as have been found by the Courts below.

parties:
Mahmuda Khatun-------Appellants
VS
Hamida Begum-------Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 10-4-2017 passed by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal, in short, FMA No. 56 of 2016 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and order dated 6-10-2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka dismissing the Title Appeal No. 328 of 2010, rejecting an application under Rule 19A, Order XLI of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the Code) filed by the appellants for setting aside the order of dismissal of the appeal, directing re-admit the appeal. 

 The plaintiff-respondent herein instituted Title Suit No. 363 of 1983 before the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), fourth Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession stating, inter alia, that the land measuring an area of 1.45 acres appertaining to CS Plot No. 873/1621 of Khatian No. 586, Mouza-Senpara Porbota under Police Station-Mirpur originally belonged to Keramat Ali Mollah. While he was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the same, he died leaving behind his two sons, namely Mokim Mollah and Shamsuddin Mollah, five daughters, namely, Kulsum, Neamat, Asimon, Samiron and Shohran and a widow, named Fatema. Thus, each son got 0.281964 acre of land, each daughter got 0.140972 acre of land and the widow got 0.18125 acre of land of the said plot. Thereafter, widow-Fatema, sold her entire share to Shamsuddin Mollah on 27-6-1957. Subsequently, Shamsuddin Mollah and Azimonnessa sold 0.26 acre of land from the said plot to the plaintiff-respondent and Musammat Lutfunnessa and handed over the possession of the said land to them on 2-4-1962. The plaintiff got the possession of the western half of the 0.26 acre of land by amicable partition and constructed boundary walls as described in the schedule 'A' to the plaint. She got her name mutated in the Khatian and has been paying rent to the Government for the said land. Moreso, RS record-of-right has been correctly published in her name. The plaintiff constructed huts thereon and had been residing in a portion of the said land, letting out the other portion. While the plaintiff had been in exclusive possession and enjoyment of the suit land by exercising 16 annas right, title and interest adversely and openly to all including the defendants for more than 12 years, the defendant No. 1 forcefully entered into a portion of the suit land in the last part of October, 1981 and dispossessed the plaintiff from the 0.06(six) acre of land as described in schedule-"B" to the plaint as suit land in her absence. The defendant No.1 had no right, title and interest in the suit land but he illegally entered into 13' scheduled land. Hence, was the suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff-respondent had no locus standi for filing the suit against them, the suit was not maintainable, the plaintiff had no cause of action for filing the suit against them. The suit was barred by limitation and provisions of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel. It was further contended that the suit land originally belonged to Mokim Ali. After his death, his son Nurul Islam alias Noor Islam, defendant No. 3 and his mother-Fatema Khatoon alias Fatema Bibi inherited the same. Fatema Khatoon sold her entire land to Nurul Islam by registered Sale Deed No. 5652 dated 9-10-1963 and handed over the possession to him on the same day. Nurul Islam sold 0.07 acre of land from the Mouza Senpara Porbota, JO No. 99, SA Khatian No.691 and SA Plot No. 873/1621 to the defendant No. 1 by registered Sale Deed Nos. 1489 dated 12-4-1980, 2302 dated 12-4-1980 and 5758 dated 16-9-1980 and handed over the possession in favour of him. The defendant No.1 had constructed a residential house in his purchased land and had been residing therein along with his family. He also got mutated his name vide Mutation Case No. 738(M)80-81 dated 28-11-1980 and a separate Khatian being No. 691/35 had been opened in his name. He had been regularly paying rents to the Government. The defendants did not at all dispossess the plaintiff-respondent from the suit land and, as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The defendant No. 1, Md Shamsul Huda, filed Title Suit No. 1213 of 1981 against the plaintiff-respondent before the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Fourth Court, Dhaka, eventually the same was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 11 of 1994. The respondent herein as plaintiff, filed Title Suit No. 363 of 1983 against the defendants before the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 4th Court, Dhaka. The same was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka, which was also renumbered as Title Suit No. 10 of 1994. 

 5. The trial Court heard both the suits analogously, decreed the Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 11 of 1994 by the judgment and decree dated 31-8-2010. 

 6. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 31-8-2010 passed by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994, the appellants-defendants herein as heirs of the defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 328 of 2010 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka and it was transferred to the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka. The appeal was heard but eventually dismissed for default on 29-7-2015. Subsequently, appellants-defendants filed an application under Rule 19A, Order XLI of the Code for directing re-admission of the said title appeal before the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka which was rejected by the judgment and order dated 6-10-2015. 

 7. Against the judgment and order dated 6-10-2015 passed by the Additional District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 328 of 2010, the appellants-defendants preferred FMA No. 56 of 2016 before the High Court Division. 

 25. The judgment and order dated 10-4-2017 passed by the single Judge of the High Court Division in FMA No. 56 of 2016 affirming the judgment and order dated 29-7-2015 passed by the Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 328 of 2010 is set aside. 

 27. The Title Appeal No. 328 of 2010 is revived to its original file and number.

parties:
Shahadat Hossain Mollick (Bacchu) and another -------- Petitioners
VS
Ayesha Akter and others -------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-7 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-1-2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge (In charge), Munshigonj in Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), Munshigonj against the opposite party Nos. 1-9, as defendant for declaration of Title and SA Khatian No. 120, RS khatian No. 141 to be declared wrong and without any legal basis stating inter alia, that the property measuring 52 decimals covered by CS and SA plot No. 601 corresponding to RS plot No. 696 of Mouza-Atigaon, originally belonged to one Rojonikanto Bhattracharya who transferred the property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a patta. While said Monindra Lal Talukder was in possession and enjoyment of the same he transferred the schedule land to one Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by a registered deed of sale No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Said Yunus Mollick was in possession and enjoyment in the half share of the property measuring 26 decimals who subsequently, transferred his share by way of settlement to one Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS Said Abdul Latif Bepari while in possession and enjoyment of the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick, by a registered deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 transferred the suit property along with other non-suited property to Most. Ashura Khatun, Harun Or Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin. The said Ashura Khatun died issueless and her brother Brigadier (Rtd.) Moniruzzaman Khan succeeded her. Said Harun Or Rashid died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 8-13 and Joynal Abedin died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1-7. While the plaintiffs went to the Tahsil office on 17-3-2008 for payment of rent for the suit property came to know that SA and RS Khatian stand recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants wrongly and for such wrong entry in the khatian title of the plaintiffs have become clouded, hence, the present suit for declaration. 

 3. The defendant-opposite parties contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia, that the property in question originally belonged to Rojonikanto Bhatracharya who transferred the same to one Monindra Lal Talukder and the said Monindra Lal Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 transferred the suit property to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick in equal share. The said Jalal Uddin Mollick transferred his share in the property in favour his wife Arjumonnessa before SA operation. Accordingly, SA and RS khatian correctly recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick and Arjumonnessa. Arjumonnessa died leaving defendant Nos. 2-7 and Yunus Mollick died leaving defendant No. 1, they have been possessing the suit land amicably and the defendant No. 1 mutated her name in RS Khatian and has been possessing the suit land on payment of rent to the government. The plaintiffs have no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property, hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial court framed as many as five issues for determination of the dispute between the parties. In course of hearing the plaintiffs examined four witnesses as PWs and the defendant examined two witnesses as DWs. Both the parties filed documents in support of their claim in suit which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing the parties dismissed the suit on contest finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their title as well as possession in the suit property by its judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 before the learned District Judge, Munshigonj who upon hearing disallowed the appeal on contest by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-1-2016. At this juncture, the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay. 

 6. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate with Mr Shahjada Al Amin Kabir, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners at the very outset submit that admittedly, the suit property originally belonged to Rojonikanto Bhattacharya. CS khatian stands recorded in his name. The said Rojonikanto Bhattacharya permanently settled the suit property along with other non-suited property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a Patta and the said Monindra Lal Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 transferred the suit property to one Yunus Mollick and another Jalal Uddin Mollick in equal share. There is no dispute between the parties regarding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick. But both the courts below by making a 3rd case most unfortunately held that the parties to the suit could not satisfy the court how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. As such, both the courts below travelled beyond their jurisdiction in deciding title of Monindra Lal Talukder which was not a matter to be determined by the court below. 

 7. Mr Ali further submits that title deed of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick is of the year 1948 more than 30 years old document which was filed in original by the defendant in suit (exhibit-Ga). As per section 90 of the Evidence Act the said deed has a strong presumptive value as the same is not required to be formally proved, but both the courts below without assigning any reason what-soever unfortunately found that Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick did not acquire any title in the suit property in the absence of any explanation how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. He further submits that Yunus Mollick settled his share in the property in favour of one Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS. In support of which the plaintiffs submitted counterfoil of the rent receipt showing payment of rent to Yunus Mollick by Abdul Latif Bepari (exhibits-3 and 3ka). But the court below instead of finding genuineness of the exhibites-3 and 3ka unfortunately held that the said document generally should be remained with the owner of the property Yunus Mollick how the said document could be produced by the tenant under Yunus Mollick. He further goes to argue that the question before the court whether Abdul Latif Bepari got the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick and the document exhibits-3 and 3ka prove that Yunus Mollick accepted rent from Abdul Latif Bepari by issuing rent receipt to him. Mr Ali further goes to submit that Abdul Latif Bepari while in possession and enjoyment of the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick transferred the same to Most. Ashura Khatun, Harun-or-Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin the predecessor of the plaintiffs by a registered sale deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 (exhibit-5). 

 8. The trial court observed that the said deed of sale has not been proved by the plaintiffs by calling the concern volume form the registry office and as such, the plaintiffs could not prove their title in the property by the aforesaid sale deed. In this regard he submits that in the absence of any contrary thing a registered document cannot be disbelieved by the court that it was not duly executed and registered and by the said deed the property was not transferred. Moreover, the deed in question of the year 1956 and an old document acquired a presumptive value under the law since nothing could produce from defence side contrary to the document of the plaintiffs. However, before the appellate court the plaintiff-appellants filed an application for calling the concern volume of the deed in question from the registry office. The appellate court upon hearing rejected the application on 17-9-2015 holding that since the learned Advocate for the respondent admitted the existence of the sale deed dated 30-3-1956 there is no need to call the volume of the deed from the registry office. Therefore, the appellate court ought to have found that the deed of the year 1956 exhibit-5 is a valid deed and by the said deed the plaintiffs acquired title through their predecessor. He further submits that mere record of right in the name of some person does not ipso facto create title in their favour. But the court below relying on the record of right in the name of defendant and also observing that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the property, dismissed the suit as well as disallowed the appeal. 

 9. Mr Mohammad Ahasan, with Mr SM Ariful Islam, learned Advocates appearing for the opposite parties submit that there is no dispute that the properties belonged to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by purchase in the year 1948. But the fact is that Yunus Mollick never transferred his share in the property to Abdul Latif Bepari or anybody by way of settlement as alleged by the plaintiffs. He further submits that in the absence of any valid deed or documents showing settlement in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari, said Abdul Latif Bepari cannot transfer the property to Most. Ashura Khatun and two others. As such, by the deed dated 30-3-1956 the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the property in question and both the courts below rightly held that the plaintiffs could not prove their title by producing any valid document. He further argued that the plaintiffs filed two counterfoils of rent receipt to prove settlement in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari showing that Yunus Mollick on receipt of rent issued rent receipt in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari. But the plaintiffs could not produce any rent receipt issued to Abdul Latif Bepari and as such, both the courts below rightly observed that it is not at all conceivable by any means that a tenant can hold a counterfoil of rent receipt issued by his landlord Yunus Mollick. 

 10. Mr Ahasan further submits that the sale deed dated 30-3-1956 exhibit-5 is a certified copy obtained by the plaintiffs from the concern registry office on 19-3-2008 and the plaintiffs did not prove the said document by calling respective volume from the concern registry office. Moreover, the plaintiffs failed to prove that the suit property was settled by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari. As such, by the said deed executed by Addul Latif Bepari the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the property. He further submits that in the absence of any valid document of transfer of the property in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari, the plaintiffs cannot say that said Abdul Latif Bepari acquired title in the property to be sold to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. He further submits that the defendant No. 1 as daughter of Yunus Mollick inherited the property and accordingly, SA and RS khatians stand recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick with the wife of another owner Jalal Uddin Mollick. He further goes to submit that the relevant khatian of the property, payment of rent by the defendant proved that the defendants acquired title in the property by inheritance and have been possessing the suit property more than statutory period of limitation on payment of rents to the government. As such, both the courts below rightly found that the plaintiffs by any evidence both oral and documentary could not prove their title and possession in the suit property. Finally, he submits that this is a suit for simple declaration and both the courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the property, as such, the suit is not maintainable in its present form without prayer for recovery of possession. 11. Heard the learned Advocates for both the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary adduced and marked as exhibits before the trial court and impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

 12. From perusal of plaint and written statement, it appears that both the parties unequivocally admitted and declared that the property in question, originally belonged to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by purchase vide sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Both the courts below in finding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick observed that the said two persons purchased the property from one Monindra Lal Talukder, but both the parties to the suit in their plaint and written statement failed to give any explanation or fact how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. I have gone through the registered deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 filed in original by the defendant No. 1 (exhibit-Ga) and a certified copy of the same by the plaintiff (exhibit-4) and from perusal of both the exhibits it appears that in the recital of the said deed it has been clearly mentioned that Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property by way of permanent settlement by a registered patta dated 25 Magh 1344 corresponding to 8-2-1938. But this pertinent facts missed the notices of the trial court as well as appellate court below. 

 13. Moreover, where there is no dispute between the parties regarding acquisition of title by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick why the trial court as well as the appellate court shall decide a question not raised before it by any party whatsoever. Therefore, this Court finds that the findings and observation of the courts below in respect of acquisition of title by Monindra, thereafter, by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick is totally contrary to the actual state of affairs. The trial court as well as the appellate court in deciding title of Abdul Latif Bepari in the suit property held that the plaintiffs could not produce any document showing settlement of the property in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari by Yunus Mollick, but they could file two counterfoils of rent receipt exhibit-3 and 3ka which ought to have remained in the possession of Yunus Mollick as Zaminder and this cannot come before the court from the custody of the plaintiffs as their vendor Abdul Latif Bepari was a tenant under Yunus Mollick and also held that Abdul Latif Bepari did not acquire any title in the absence of any patta and he could not transfer the property to Most. Ashura Khatun and two others by a registered deed dated 30-3-1956 (exhibit-5). I have gone through the (exhibit-3 and 3ka), it appears that the suit property was settled by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS. 

 15. Both the courts below while dismissing the suit as well as disallowing the appeal failed to consider those documentary evidences produced by the parties to the suit in its true perspective and without going through the contents of the exhibits most unfortunately disbelieved the exhibits 4 and 5 both are registered document of the year 1948 and 1956, more than 30 years old. Apart from this, this Court finds that the observations and finding of both the courts below are totally contrary to the actual state of affair and based on serious misconstruction of the evidence and misconception of law. The trial court as well as the appellate court concurrently held that Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick did not acquire title in the property by the deed from Monindra Lal Talukder in the absence of any explanation how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property, which also goes against the defendants in suit. But they did not prefer any appeal against the judgment of the trial court as well as any revision against the judgment and decree of the appellate court. In this situation, question may arise how the defendant-opposite parties can defend themself before the appellate court as well as this Court where their title also negated by the judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

 16. In this precarious situation, this Court is to observe that this suit is of the plaintiffs not the defendants and according to law the plaintiffs are to prove their case and no benefit can be taken from the weakness of the defence. Where the plaintiffs by submitting documentary evidences namely, registered kabala dated 16-3-1948 and registered kabala dated 30-3-1956 could establish that the property owned by Yunus Mollick thereafter, Abdul Latif Bepari and lastly, by Ashura Khatun, Harun Or Rashid and Joynal Abedin the suit property ought to have recorded in the names of Ashura Khatun and two others but the property stands recorded in the name of Yunus Mollick who happens to be the husband of Ashura Khatun and vendor of Abdul Latif Bepari. Recording of name of Yunus Mollick in SA and RS khatian, in my opinion, is not so fatal because Yunus Mollick was the vendor of Abdul Latif from whom Ahsura Khatun and two others purchased the same. And, for such recording, it cannot be said that Yunus Mollick never transferred the property to anybody or the defendant No. 1 acquired any title in the property on the basis of record of right. Both the courts below failed to notice the fact that mere recording of khatian in the name of vendor does not ipso facto create title in favour of the defendant No. 1 or any other defendants. It is also found that the defendant No. 1 got her name mutated in the khatian as her father's name was appearing in the record of right. Mere mutation in the khatian also cannot create any title in favour of any person without any basis. 

 17. In the present case the plaintiffs could able to prove their title, right from Monindra Lal Talukder to Ashura Khatun and two others by successive transfers vide exhibites-3, 3ka, 4 and 5. Therefore, the trial court ought to have decreed the suit and the appellate court also misdirected himself in not considering the evidences both oral and documentary. I have gone through the evidences adduced by the parties as PWs and DWs. Though the PWs could not specifically tell the boundary of the property as well as the quantum of land in the plot it does not mean that the plaintiffs are not in possession as well as the DWs also could not substantiate their claim by oral evidence that they have been possessing the same specifically, exclusively ousting the plaintiffs in suit. Where the plaintiffs could prove their title in the suit property and in the absence of clear evidence and exclusive possession of the defendants in the suit property the plaintiffs need not pray for any consequential relief by way of recovery of possession. 

 21. The impugned judgment and decreed dated 14-1-2016 passed by the learned District Judge, Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 126 of 2012 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25-9-2012 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), Munshigonj, in Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 are hereby set aside. Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 is hereby decreed in favour of the plaintiffs.

parties:
Zakir Hossain and another
Vs.
Md. Yousuf Kabir and another
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: This appeal has arisen out of the leave granted on 14.03.2011 in Civil Review Petition No.90 of 2010 directed against the judgment and order dated 06.05.2010 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1359 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.181 of 2004 affirming those dated 13.05.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.59 of 1994. 

 3. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.59 of 1994 and Money Suit No.2 of 2002 in the Second Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Title Suit No.59 of 1994 was for declaration of their title to the suit land; recovery of khas possession; for further declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 by the Subordinate Judge, third Court, Dhaka; also for declaration that the kabala executed through Court on 27.02.1980 in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void and same is not binding upon the plaintiffs and for permanent injunction. 

 4. Their specific case, in short, was that the land measuring an area of .0568 acre appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.241, C.S. Plot No.390/3940, S.A. Khatian No.197, S.A. Plot No.555, R.S. Khatian No.1511, 1522 and R.S. Plot No.1263 of Lalbag Mouza, Touzi No.61/1, Ward No.7, Sheet No.10, District-Dhaka, as described in the schedule to the plaint originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya. The suit property was sold in auction for arrear of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and the same was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and the sale certificate was issued on 19.11.1953. Possession of the suit land was delivered on 20.01.1954 to the auction purchaser. Ali Ahmed got his name mutated in the Khatian and paid rent to the Government. S.A. Khatian No.197 and R.S. Khatian No.1248 were prepared in his name. He died on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, namely, Khatibunnessa, who inherited the entire suit property as his heir and as per provision of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnessa died on 10.02.1978 leaving her only brother Abdul Mannan, who inherited her entire property including the suit property. He transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 29.11.1979. Thus, the plaintiffs became owners of the suit property. The defendants forged some papers and tried to take over possession of the suit property forcibly but due to intervention of the respectable people of the locality, they could not take over possession of the same. On 06.07.1980, the defendants along with a process server of the Court and police tried to take over the possession of suit property again but the plaintiffs, by showing decree of the court, resisted them. After holding inquiry from the bailiff of the Court, the plaintiffs' father, Abdul Majid, came to know that the defendants had obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the basis of an agreement dated 12.06.1972 executed by Rasheda Begum. Rasheda Begum had no title and possession in the suit land and, therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title on the basis of the decree. The defendants got a kabala deed executed and registered in their names through Court in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979. Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in the said suit. Therefore, the decree passed in the said suit is not binding upon them. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.329 of 1980 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction, which was decreed on 28.03.1984 on contest. Against which, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.196 of 1984 and, on transfer, the same was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal on 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.76 of 1987 in the High Court Division but the rule was discharged on 27.05.1992. Then the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.297 of 1992 in the Appellate Division, and the same was also dismissed. On 27.10.1993, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the Title Execution Case No.3 of 1980, arising out of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 which was rejected on 29.01.1994. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs, they declared that they would soon dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property. The cause of action of the suit arose on 21.10.1993 when the defendants along with the bailiff of the Court asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them. When the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing, the defendants along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons, entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.1997 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom. They looted away the household articles worth of Tk.6,00,000/-, and also looted the goods of his tenants of the suit premises and took over possession of the same. The defendants deprived the plaintiffs from getting rent of their tenants. After that incident, Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs, lodged a First Information Report with Lalbagh Police Station under Section 144/447/448 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants, one Wazir Ahmed also lodged an FIR with the said police station which was registered as Lalbagh P.S. Case No.940 dated 16/09/1997. Thereafter, the defendants, by making threat to the plaintiffs and their father Abdul Majid, took signature in a white paper and prepared a money receipt of 16,60,000/-. The defendants demolished the one storied building and the shop rooms situated in the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. So, they are entitled to get mesne profit. In the premises, the plaintiffs filed Money Suit No.2 of 2002 claiming Tk.28,71,900/- with interest and cost. 

 5. The defendant-appellants contested the suits by filing written statements. Their case, in short, was that the suit property of No.1 Atash Khana Lane, along with other property owned by Khiroda Shundari Daishya. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa by a registered kabala dated 27/03/1953 and delivered possession. Salimunnesa transferred her 8(eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8(eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15/06/1959, Ilias, by a registered deed of gift, transferred his said 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16 (sixteen) annas owner and possessor of the suit property. One Munjurul Hoq was tenant in a portion of the suit property. He defaulted to pay rent. Accordingly, Rasheda filed Money Suit No.50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for the realization of arrear rent. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 for eviction of Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. The tenant, forging signatures of Rasheda Begum, filed two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively in the said money suit and House Rent case and obtained compromise decrees. Knowing about the same, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No.221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deeds of agreement dated 16/11/1959 as well compromise petitions filed in Money Suit No.50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 and for setting aside those fraudulent compromise decrees.
